writing.modelEssay:
While striving for the Chinese Dream, young people enjoy more opportunities to realize their self-worth. As
the nation advances, doors that were once closed are swinging open for the younger generation. Specifically,
the rapid growth of technology, education and entrepreneurship offers a broad stage on which youth can turn
their talents into real contributions.
These opportunities become meaningful only when young people seize them actively. Take my cousin as an
example: instead of chasing a comfortable office job, she founded a start-up that brings online courses to rural
children. For instance, thousands of students now learn from teachers they could never have met, and she has
found genuine value in her work. In this way, personal ambition and national progress reinforce each other.
In a word, the Chinese Dream is not a distant slogan but a living platform that lets every young person shine.
As long as we combine individual effort with the tide of the times, we can both realize our self-worth and push
the country forward.
writing.modelCn:
在为中国梦奋斗的同时，年轻人享有更多实现自我价值的机会。随着国家的发展，曾经紧闭的大门正向年
青一代敞开。具体来说，科技、教育与创业的迅速成长，提供了一个广阔的舞台，让青年得以把才华转化
为切实的贡献。
这些机会只有在青年主动抓住时才有意义。以我的表姐为例：她没有去追求一份安稳的办公室工作，而是
创办了一家为乡村孩子送去网络课程的初创企业。举例来说，如今成千上万的学生得以师从他们本来永远
无法遇见的老师，而她也在工作中找到了真正的价值。就这样，个人抱负与国家进步彼此成就。
总而言之，中国梦不是一句遥远的口号，而是一个让每个年轻人都能发光的鲜活舞台。只要我们把个人的
努力汇入时代的潮流，就既能实现自我价值，又能推动国家前行。

translation.source: 尊老是中华民族的传统美德，深深植根于中国人的思想和行为中，是人们普遍遵守的行为规范和社会准则。在当今的中国，这种美德得到广泛传承。社会各界积极营造敬老助老的社会氛围。为老年人提供便利服务已成为社会共识，例如社区专门开设长者食堂，公共场所配置优先座位。政府还出台了一系列政策，为老年人的权益提供有力保障。尊老是社会和谐与发展的重要基石，有助于培育良好的社会氛围，推动整个社会文明进步。
translation.reference: Respecting the elderly is a traditional virtue of the Chinese nation. Deeply rooted in the thoughts and behavior of the Chinese people, it is a code of conduct and a social norm that people widely observe. In China today, this virtue is widely carried forward. People from all walks of life actively foster a social atmosphere of respecting and helping the elderly. Providing convenient services for the elderly has become a social consensus. For example, communities open special canteens for the elderly, and public places provide priority seats. The government has also introduced a series of policies, providing strong protection for the rights and interests of the elderly. Respecting the elderly is an important cornerstone of social harmony and development, helping to foster a sound social atmosphere and promote the civilized progress of the whole society.

cloze.passage: By now, it is generally accepted that regular exercise comes with an assortment of health benefits for people who maintain the habit over time. But is it __26__ too late to start? New research looked at people who increased their exercise levels after their 40s beyond levels they had when they were younger and those individuals showed declines in their risk of early __27__ which were similar to those of people who exercised consistently throughout their lives. This was a __28__ of 32% to 35% compared to people who did not exercise. Those who began exercising in middle age also saw reductions in their incidence of __29__ diseases, such as heart disease and cancer, which were similar to the steady exercisers. So why bother exercising consistently throughout your life? The authors of the study __30__ that some might interpret the study’s findings to mean that they can delay starting an exercise program but this would be a mistake. There are other benefits, both mental and physical, to staying consistently active that we should not __31__ . These real health benefits include better __32__ functioning and lowered risk of gaining weight. The latter is __33__ important given the global obesity epidemic. In addition, experts assert that starting younger is better because, if you make a habit of exercising when you are young, you are more likely to keep up those __34__ later in life. It is ideal, then, for people to start exercising when they are children or __35__ , and it is good to maintain an active lifestyle at all times regardless of your age. However, this study does indicate that, if you have not been active, you can still benefit if you start becoming active in your 40s and 50s.

26.explanation: ever 与 too…to 在疑问句中构成 "是否真的太……以至于不能……" 的强调 But is it __(26)__ too late to start? 是承接 "运动有诸多益处" 后的设问：是否"真的"太晚 了？ever 在疑问句中作副词，与 too late 连用强调"究竟、真的"，自然过渡到第二段用研 究数据回应这个疑问。

27.explanation: risk of early mortality = 早死风险，是流行病学固定表述 declines in their risk of early __(27)__ 描述"早死风险的下降"，early mortality（早死） 是公共卫生研究的标准术语；第二段后文又提 reductions in their incidence of __(29)__ diseases 谈疾病发病率，整段就是"死亡风险 + 疾病风险"双线索。

28.explanation: drop of 32% to 35% = "32% 到 35% 的下降" 上文 declines in their risk of early __(27)__ 用到 declines（下降）；本句 This was a __(28)__ of 32% to 35% 的 This 就指代那个 decline，drop 与 decline 同义对接"下降 幅度"。

29.explanation: such as heart disease and cancer 是 chronic diseases 的典型例证 原文 reductions in their incidence of __(29)__ diseases, such as heart disease and cancer——心脏病与癌症都是医学上的典型"慢性病"（chronic diseases）。such as 后的 例子直接锁死形容词的语义指向。

30.explanation: concede 承认"研究结论可能被误读"这一让步语气 上下文 The authors of the study __(30)__ that some might interpret the study's findings to mean that they can delay starting an exercise program but this would be a mistake. 是研究作者主动承认"有人可能会误读"——这是不利于研究主张的让步，再用 but this would be a mistake 反驳。concede（承认不利事实）正是这种"先让步、后反 驳"的标志性动词。

31.explanation: disregard the benefits = 忽视这些好处 There are other benefits, both mental and physical, to staying consistently active that we should not __(31)__.——"还有其他身心益处是我们不应当 ___ 的"，逻辑要的 是"忽视"；disregard the benefits 是惯用搭配，且与下文 These real health benefits include better cognitive functioning and lowered risk of gaining weight. 顺承——正 因为不应忽视，所以列举出来。

32.explanation: cognitive functioning 是"认知功能"的固定搭配 better __(32)__ functioning and lowered risk of gaining weight 列举运动的真实健康好 处——"更好的认知功能"与"降低增重风险"并列；cognitive functioning 是医学/心理学常 用术语，正合此处。

33.explanation: given the global obesity epidemic 提供了"尤其"的现实背景 The latter is __(33)__ important given the global obesity epidemic.——"鉴于全球肥 胖流行病"这个背景子句直接为前面提供"尤其重要"的理由；particularly 与背景子句一拍 即合。

34.explanation: those patterns 回指前句的 "make a habit of exercising" if you make a habit of exercising when you are young, you are more likely to keep up those __(34)__ later in life. 中 those 指代前面的 "运动这种习惯"，patterns（模式/习 惯）正好对接 habit；keep up patterns（保持这些模式/习惯）也是日常搭配。

Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2. Restaurants Are Now Employing Robots — Should Chefs Be Worried? A) Like most chefs, Flippy is not afraid of hard work. J.cn: 餐饮业目前正遭受熟练厨师的严重短缺——根据技能机构People 1st的数据,缺口为1.1万人。"旨在使 流程更加简单易行的自动化系统正试图弥合这一差距,"《餐厅》杂志编辑Stefan Chomka说。

K.en: In terms of simplifying or enhancing the customer experience, online restaurant booking has been the easily- won success of the internet age. Automated at-table ordering and payment is seen as the next landmark. Until then, early adopters, such as the Manchester bar owner Andy Smith, who uses the Ordoo app at his venue 33 Oldham Street, may well experience growing but "lower than expected" acceptance.
K.cn: 就简化或增强顾客体验而言,在线餐厅预订一直是互联网时代轻松获得的成功。桌边自动点餐和支付被 视为下一个里程碑。在那之前,早期采用者,如曼彻斯特酒吧老板Andy Smith,他在其场所33 Oldham Street使用Ordoo应用程序,很可能会经历不断增长但"低于预期"的接受度。

L.en: Embarrassing failures in restaurant tech frequently hit the headlines. The TGI Fridays drone (无人机) that injured a Brooklyn Daily photographer; US burger chain Shake Shack having to retreat from plans for entirely cashless ordering sites. But, says Chomka, such technology could miss the mark if it only offers "solutions to problems that don't really exist". "Payments being automatic" could be useful, he adds. But, in an expensive restaurant, "how quick do you need dinner to be?"
L.cn: 餐厅技术中的尴尬失败经常登上头条。TGI Fridays的无人机伤害了Brooklyn Daily的摄影师;美国汉堡 连锁店Shake Shack不得不放弃完全无现金点餐站点的计划。但是,Chomka说,如果这种技术只提 供"对实际上不存在的问题的解决方案",它可能会偏离目标。他补充说,"支付自动化"可能是有用的。但 是,在一家昂贵的餐厅,"你需要晚餐有多快?"

M.en: That attachment to the human art of hospitality will be heartening for staff who see automation as a threat to jobs. "Unite is concerned that without safeguards, any benefits will bypass workers in low-paying jobs, such as waiters," says the union's London regional officer, Dave Turnbull. "We're urging Members of Parliament to ensure automation does not just benefit a wealthy few like previous industrial revolutions."
M.cn: 对人类待客艺术的这种依恋将让那些将自动化视为工作威胁的员工感到鼓舞。"Unite担心,如果没有保 障措施,任何好处都将绕过低薪工作的工人,如服务员,"该工会的伦敦地区官员Dave Turnbull说。"我们 敦促国会议员确保自动化不会像以前的工业革命那样只让少数富人受益。"

N.en: The industry principle is that automation will allow it to redeploy staff more effectively. Jobs will change, if not immediately decrease in number. "Self-order screens mean more demand for people front-of-house. Last year, we recruited 1,000 new managers," says McDonald's COO, Jason Clark. Caliburger has a programme to retrain staff as robot engineers or "chef techs".
N.cn: 行业原则是自动化将使其能够更有效地重新部署员工。工作将发生变化,即使数量不会立即减少。"自 助点餐屏幕意味着对前台人员的更多需求。去年,我们招聘了1000名新经理,"麦当劳首席运营官Jason Clark说。Caliburger有一个项目将员工重新培训为机器人工程师或"厨师技术员"。

O.en: But ultimately the chance to reduce overheads (管理费用) by employing fewer people or at lower rates will be what attracts big brands to technology. Invariably, over the next 10 years, jobs will go in conventional bricks- built restaurants, not least because automation will boost their rapidly growing rival: delivery. Companies such as Domino and Just Eat have both experimented with robot and drone delivery, which is already legal in Reykjavik, Iceland. "Robot food deliveries are the future," says Noel Sharkey. "Small, 4 mph ground robots are safe and will work 24 hours a day."
O.cn: 但最终,通过雇用更少的人或以更低的薪酬来减少管理费用的机会将是吸引大品牌采用技术的原因。在 未来10年,传统实体餐厅的工作岗位将不可避免地减少,尤其是因为自动化将促进其快速增长的竞争对 手:配送。Domino和Just Eat等公司都尝试过机器人和无人机配送,这在冰岛雷克雅未克已经合法。"机 器人食品配送是未来,"Noel Sharkey说。"小型、时速4英里的地面机器人是安全的,将24小时工作。"

P.en: Combined with machine learning of anticipated order volumes and the minute-by-minute cooking data generated by systems such as QSR, that robot fleet could deliver almost instantly. "Restaurants will prepare food ahead of orders coming in," predicts Just Eat's director of engineering, Daniel Richardson. "I'll be able to say 'Let's have pizza' to my family, my intelligent assistant will hear and 10 minutes later the food will be at my door." No one is putting an exact date on it yet. But in the dining room and on your doorstep, the robots are coming.
P.cn: 结合对预期订单量的机器学习以及QSR等系统生成的逐分钟烹饪数据,该机器人车队几乎可以即时配 送。"餐厅将在订单到来之前准备食物,"Just Eat的工程总监Daniel Richardson预测。"我可以对我的

paragraphs.en: Many see friendships as a comfort blanket: a shoulder to cry on, a reliable soul to confide in. However, more often than not, in our eagerness to seek individual success, we lose friends along the way and that has become part of the process.
paragraphs.cn: 许多人将友谊视为一条慰藉的毛毯:一个可以倾诉的肩膀,一个可以信赖的灵魂。然而,更多时候,在我们急于 追求个人成功的过程中,我们沿途失去了朋友,而这已成为这一过程的一部分。

paragraphs.en: The chaos and never-ending turmoil that accompanies everyday life is an aggressive obstacle in the pursuit of stable friendships. As students, we use this excuse to shrug off losing people who we once thought to be loved ones.
paragraphs.cn: 伴随日常生活而来的混乱和永无止境的动荡是追求稳定友谊的严重障碍。作为学生,我们用这个借口来对失 去那些我们曾经认为是挚爱之人的事实不以为意。

paragraphs.en: Instead of viewing our lives as a race, where everyone is on their own path to some form of success, we must relearn to value the connections we make along the track. We must reevaluate the harm of radical, individual freedom.
paragraphs.cn: 我们不应该将生活视为一场竞赛,每个人都在通往某种形式成功的自己的道路上,而必须重新学会珍视我们 在这条轨道上建立的联系。我们必须重新评估激进的个人自由所带来的危害。

paragraphs.en: Radical individualism elevates the freedom of the individual over the collective. It argues, for instance, that universal healthcare, an example of collectivism, threatened the dream of many Americans.
paragraphs.cn: 激进个人主义将个人自由置于集体之上。例如,它认为全民医疗保健这一集体主义的例子威胁到了许多美国 人的梦想。

paragraphs.en: Many of us have fallen victim to an individualistic culture. Society tends to celebrate personal achievement and commend it based on the assumption that winning or succeeding is a consequence of working harder than the next person.
paragraphs.cn: 我们中的许多人已经成为个人主义文化的受害者。社会倾向于颂扬个人成就,并基于这样的假设对其进行赞 扬:获胜或成功是比别人更努力工作的结果。

paragraphs.en: As a society, we idolize the concept of "losing friends on the road to success". I remember hearing in high school, "Don't worry about losing friendships, just focus on study and getting into college. That's all that will matter in the long run," a sentiment that is not unique to my experience. It's preached in many success stories, and it's embedded in the way we see growth. Motivational speakers will push their audience to be complacent to the inevitable end of losing friends. Spend too much time with friends? You're losing time better utilized on your achievements. Invest time in your relationships? Invest time in your work instead.
paragraphs.cn: 作为一个社会,我们崇拜"在通往成功的路上失去朋友"这一概念。我记得在高中时听到过:"不要担心失去友 谊,只需专注于学习和考上大学。从长远来看,那才是唯一重要的事情。"这种情绪并非我独有的经历。它在 许多成功故事中被宣扬,并且嵌入在我们看待成长的方式中。励志演讲者会推动他们的听众对失去朋友这一 不可避免的结局感到满足。花太多时间和朋友在一起?你正在浪费本可以更好地用于你的成就上的时间。 在你的人际关系上投入时间?把时间投入到你的工作上吧。

paragraphs.en: This constant need to succeed has blinded us from seeing through the whirlwind of change that accompanies our everyday lives. We are expected to tangibly succeed, earn awards, get higher positions, earn better grades. In order to succeed, we lose friends, and that has sadly become normalized.
paragraphs.cn: 这种对成功的持续需求使我们看不清伴随日常生活而来的变化旋涡。我们被期望取得有形的成功,赢得奖 项,获得更高的职位,取得更好的成绩。为了成功,我们失去了朋友,而这已可悲地变得正常化了。

paragraphs.en: We cannot be complacent with losing friendships because they are our anchors. Yes, pursue success. Challenge yourself. Push limits. But contrary to all the self-proclaimed success experts, doing it alone does not make you more successful or any better than someone who achieved it with the help of others.
paragraphs.cn: 我们不能对失去友谊感到满足,因为它们是我们的锚。是的,追求成功。挑战自己。突破极限。但与所有 那些自封的成功专家相反,独自做到这一点并不会让你更成功,也不会让你比在他人帮助下实现它的人更 优秀。

paragraphs.en: Put effort into fostering healthy relationships, and maintaining them through your busy schedule that seems like it leaves no time for anyone else. Although we may be living in a society that treasures the independent pursuit of achievement, having people to support and love you on the way is far more important than any end result.
paragraphs.cn: 努力培养健康的人际关系,并在你那似乎不为任何其他人留出时间的繁忙日程中维持这些关系。尽管我们可 能生活在一个珍视独立追求成就的社会中,但在这条路上有人支持和爱你远比任何最终结果都重要得多。

paragraphs.en: During his acceptance speech for the Nobel Peace Prize, Martin Luther King Jr. said, "I believe that unarmed truth and unconditional love will have the final word in reality."
paragraphs.cn: 在诺贝尔和平奖获奖感言中,小马丁·路德·金说:"我相信,手无寸铁的真理和无条件的爱在现实中终将获胜。"

paragraphs.en: More than five decades later, our society is still struggling to separate truth from fantasy, fact from fiction. From disputes over the climate change to debates about how slavery is taught, America is at a crossroads. And the battle for equity is at the heart of these vital conversations.
paragraphs.cn: 五十多年后,我们的社会仍在努力区分真实与幻想、事实与虚构。从关于气候变化的争论到关于如何教授奴 隶制的辩论,美国正处于十字路口。而公平之战正是这些重要对话的核心。

paragraphs.en: Study after study shows that inequity has had appalling consequences. A 2020 report by Citi indicated that "Black students could have increased their lifetime incomes $90 - $113 billion" if equity issues related to higher education had been adequately addressed over the past two decades.
paragraphs.cn: 一项又一项研究表明,不公平已经造成了骇人的后果。花旗集团2020年的一份报告指出,"如果过去二十年高 等教育相关的公平问题得到充分解决,黑人学生本可以增加900亿至1130亿美元的终身收入"。

paragraphs.en: This statistic represents a flood of issues we've failed to confront as a nation. It also highlights one truth: We're missing out on valuable opportunities to bridge the differences that divide us. However, by honoring King's legacy, we can get our country back on the path toward true equity.
paragraphs.cn: 这一统计数据代表着我们作为一个国家未能直面的大量问题。它也凸显了一个真相:我们正在错失弥合分歧 的宝贵机会。然而,通过传承马丁·路德·金的遗志,我们可以让国家重回通往真正公平的道路。

paragraphs.en: Students - and adults for that matter - simply cannot understand the conflicts we have today without understanding what caused them in the first place. That means we have a responsibility to help them make connections between US history and current events. It also means giving them the tools they need to address inequity and bias in their own lives. Adherence to these principles, along with a commitment to truthful dialogue, can help every student better appreciate how far we've come and more clearly see the roads we have yet to travel.
paragraphs.cn: 学生——以及成年人——如果不理解最初导致冲突的原因,就根本无法理解我们今天面临的冲突。这意味 着我们有责任帮助他们在美国历史与时事之间建立联系。这也意味着要给他们提供在自己生活中应对不公 平和偏见所需的工具。遵循这些原则,加上对真实对话的承诺,可以帮助每个学生更好地认识到我们已经走 了多远,并更清楚地看到我们尚未踏上的道路。

paragraphs.en: With more truthful analysis of the need for more qualified, diverse educators, we can improve our recruiting, training, and retention strategies for schools across the country.
paragraphs.cn: 通过更真实地分析对更多合格的、多元化教育工作者的需求,我们可以改进全国各地学校的招聘、培训和留 用策略。

paragraphs.en: Unfortunately, our deeply rooted divisions are delaying these advancements. A recent survey found that 77 percent of Americans believe the nation is "more divided than ever before". But reports of increased polarization shouldn't persuade us to look away from one another. Instead, they should compel us to address our shared issues head-on.
paragraphs.cn: 不幸的是,我们根深蒂固的分歧正在延缓这些进步。最近的一项调查发现,77%的美国人认为国家"比以往任 何时候都更加分裂"。但关于两极分化加剧的报道不应说服我们将目光从彼此身上移开。相反,它们应该促 使我们正面应对我们共同的问题。

paragraphs.en: We are not, as some would suggest, living in a "post-racial society". We simply cannot afford to keep our heads buried in the sand when it comes to racial inequity. Unless we get honest about intolerance, bias, and how these social diseases impact the ways we treat one another, injustice will continue to haunt us. But our children and our grandchildren deserve better.
paragraphs.cn: 正如一些人所暗示的,我们并非生活在一个"后种族社会"。在种族不平等问题上,我们根本无法继续将头埋 在沙子里。除非我们诚实面对不宽容、偏见,以及这些社会疾病如何影响我们彼此对待的方式,否则不公正 将继续困扰我们。但我们的子孙后代应该得到更好的未来。

paragraphs.en: On this Martin Luther King Day and beyond, let's commit to working together to disrupt the status quo. Let's continue to build a better, more inclusive nation; and in the words of Martin Luther King Jr., "A society at peace with itself, a society that can live with its conscience."
paragraphs.cn: 在这个马丁·路德·金日以及之后的日子里,让我们致力于共同努力打破现状。让我们继续建设一个更美好、 更包容的国家;用小马丁·路德·金的话说,"一个与自身和平相处的社会,一个能够心安理得的社会。"

It's for this reason that I don't know anything on this matter beyond what we can all read in the newspapers.

segments.speaker: W

segments.speaker: M

segments.en: One thing I've learned in a quarter-century of management is that there are ample gray areas in human behavior, and that there may not always be clear right-or-wrong solutions to employee disputes. When two people have different versions of the same event, it can be hard to know whom to believe. One such circumstance always comes back to me. It happened years ago, and it's a measure of the forgettable nature of the conflict that I no longer even recall what the dispute was about, but I definitely recall the resolution. Two talented young executives, one of whom I was managing, had vastly different accounts of the same event, and it seemed likely we'd never get to the truth. We reached the deadlock, and the manager of the other individual said, "Here's something I learned from an excellent manager I once worked for. He used to say, 'When in doubt, assume positive intent.'" And just like that, we had a path forward. My counterpart and I agreed we might never ascertain the actual facts of the matter; quite likely there were elements of truth in both employees' stories. We agreed to monitor their actions and relationship going forward, but to intervene no further. We assumed the best about both of them and moved on. The result was that we were able to put the conflict behind us. In fact, their problems didn't recur. Over the years, this general approach has proved useful. Whenever the truth is obscure, assuming positive intent and agreeing to move on can be a constructive decision.
segments.cn: 在担任管理职务的25年里,我学到的一点是,人类行为中存在大量灰色地带,对于员工纠纷可能并不总是有明 确的对错解决方案。当两个人对同一事件有不同的说法时,很难知道该相信谁。有一件事总让我记忆犹新。 那是多年前发生的,这场冲突之所以容易被遗忘,以至于我现在甚至不记得争议是关于什么的,但我确实记得 解决方法。两位才华横溢的年轻主管,其中一位由我管理,对同一事件有截然不同的说法,而且似乎我们永远 也无法查明真相。我们陷入了僵局,另一位员工的经理说:'有件事是我从曾经共事过的一位优秀经理那里学 到的。他常说,当你有疑问时,假设对方有善意。'就这样,我们有了前进的方向。我的同事和我一致认为,我们 可能永远无法确定事情的真实情况;很可能两位员工的说法中都有真实的成分。我们同意今后监督他们的行 为和关系,但不再进一步介入。我们对他们两人都做了最好的假设,然后继续前进。结果是我们能够把冲突 抛在身后。事实上,他们的问题没有再次出现。多年来,这种总体方法被证明是有用的。每当真相模糊不清 时,假设积极意图并同意继续前进可能是一个建设性的决定。

segments.en: For some Americans, going out to dinner is a treat, planned and budgeted for. For others, it's just a daily occurrence. And that second group of people is becoming the majority as the number of Americans who enjoy cooking is declining. In the early 2000s, researcher Eddie Yoon conducted a survey to ascertain Americans' attitudes to cooking. The survey found that 15% of Americans loved to cook, 50% said they hated to cook and 35% reported mixed feelings. When Yoon conducted the same survey 15 years later, only 10% of respondents reported a love of cooking, 45% said they hated it and 45% had mixed feelings. Yoon asserts cooking is akin to sewing. As recently as the early 20th century, many Americans sewed their own clothing. Today, the vast majority of Americans buy clothing; only a tiny minority still sew, and they do it mainly as a hobby. Yoon believes the number of home cooks will diminish in a similar fashion. Currently, the average American household spends over $3,000 per year on dining out. However, what people save in convenience, they lose in cash. Take buying lunch on workdays for example. People spend, on average, $10 per meal when they buy lunch. Making your own lunch, meanwhile, will cost less. One survey found people only spend on average $6.30 when they bring lunch prepared at home. Americans' growing aversion to spending time in the kitchen signifies a host of challenges for the grocery industry. It's likely to detrimentally impact family finances as well.
segments.cn: 对于一些美国人来说,外出就餐是一种享受,需要计划和预算。对于另一些人来说,这只是日常活动。随着喜 欢烹饪的美国人数量下降,第二类人正在成为多数。在21世纪初,研究员Eddie Yoon进行了一项调查,以了解 美国人对烹饪的态度。调查发现,15%的美国人热爱烹饪,50%的人表示讨厌烹饪,35%的人感觉复杂。当 Yoon在15年后进行同样的调查时,只有10%的受访者表示热爱烹饪,45%的人说他们讨厌烹饪,45%的人感 觉复杂。Yoon认为烹饪类似于缝纫。就在20世纪初,许多美国人还自己缝制衣服。如今,绝大多数美国人购 买服装;只有极少数人仍在缝纫,而且他们主要把它作为一种爱好。Yoon认为家庭烹饪者的数量将以类似的 方式减少。目前,美国家庭平均每年在外出就餐上花费超过3000美元。然而,人们在便利性上节省的,却在金 钱上损失了。以工作日购买午餐为例。人们购买午餐时平均每餐花费10美元。与此同时,自己做午餐的成 本更低。一项调查发现,人们带自制午餐时平均只花费6.30美元。美国人越来越不愿意花时间在厨房,这意 味着杂货行业面临一系列挑战。这也可能对家庭财务产生不利影响。

segments.en: Every year, of the more than 2.5 billion bags checked onto flights worldwide, 26 million go missing — and of that 26 million, 1 million never make it back to their original owner. Bad weather and flight delays, miscoded destination tags and some people simply forgetting to pick up one of their bags are a few of the reasons. But the number-one reason a bag ends up lost is that it has no ID tag, and airlines don't know to whom it belongs.
segments.cn: 每年,全球超过25亿件托运行李中,有2600万件丢失——而在这2600万件中,有100万件永远无法回到原主 人手中。恶劣天气和航班延误、目的地标签编码错误以及有些人干脆忘记取其中一件行李,这些都是部分原 因。但行李最终丢失的首要原因是没有身份标签,航空公司不知道它属于谁。

segments.en: Transferring baggage from check-in to departure gates to arrival gates to baggage claim is a delicate piece of timing. If the system moves too slowly, the bags won't make connecting flights. If it's too fast, the bags may make the connection but the passengers might miss the flight. Each airport has its own way of allotting how much time a bag needs to move in transit. Some airports have sophisticated automated systems, including scanners that read baggage labels, destination-coded vehicles that load and unload the bags without stopping, and sorting machines that route baggage to the appropriate gate. Even so, all that technology may not save your baggage tag from being torn off on the conveyor belt, making you the owner of a bag with no name.
segments.cn: 将行李从值机柜台转运到出发登机口、抵达登机口再到行李提取处,是一项精细的时间把控工作。如果系统 运转太慢,行李就赶不上转机航班。如果太快,行李可能赶上了转机,但乘客可能错过航班。每个机场都有自 己的方式来分配行李在中转过程中所需的时间。一些机场拥有精密的自动化系统,包括读取行李标签的扫描 仪、无需停车即可装卸行李的目的地编码车辆,以及将行李分拣到相应登机口的分拣机。即便如此,所有这 些技术也可能无法阻止你的行李牌在传送带上被撕掉,使你成为一件无名行李的主人。

segments.en: Once a bag goes missing and the passenger files a claim, the bag is declared "mishandled" by the carrier. Mishandled refers to bags that have been delayed, lost, stolen or damaged. Most delayed bags are only one flight behind their owners and can be delivered within 24 hours. The other bags are examined by airline employees for clues to their ownership and destination. If the mystery is solved, those bags are returned to their owners within four or five days. Bags with no destination code or identification tag are shipped to a central warehouse, and undergo a comprehensive baggage tracing process over the next 90 days.
segments.cn: 一旦行李丢失且乘客提出索赔,该行李就被承运人宣布为"处理不当"。处理不当是指延误、丢失、被盗或损 坏的行李。大多数延误的行李只比其主人晚一个航班,可以在24小时内送达。其他行李则由航空公司员工 检查,寻找关于所有权和目的地的线索。如果谜团得到解决,这些行李会在四到五天内归还给主人。没有目 的地代码或身份标签的行李会被运往中央仓库,在接下来的90天内进行全面的行李追踪流程。

segments.en: Airlines inventory their mishandled baggage, and many use a database to match the contents with owners' descriptions. It takes about three months to go from "missing in action" to "irretrievably lost". Once that happens, the bags are donated to charity, sold at auction, or purchased by a company which sells them to the public.
segments.cn: 航空公司会清点处理不当的行李,许多公司使用数据库将行李内容与主人的描述进行匹配。从"失踪"到"无 法找回的丢失"大约需要三个月时间。一旦发生这种情况,这些行李会被捐赠给慈善机构、拍卖出售,或由某 家公司购买后再出售给公众。

segments.en: So never pack anything of real value in your checked baggage. And make sure your name is on the bag, along with your phone number, so an agent can contact you.
segments.cn: 因此,切勿在托运行李中装入任何真正有价值的物品。并确保你的姓名在行李上,连同你的电话号码,这样工 作人员就能联系到你。

segments.en: You've probably been with someone who ignored you while interacting with his or her smartphone. And you've probably engaged in this behavior yourself. In a recent survey, nine out of ten respondents said they'd used their smartphone during their most recent social activity. There's also evidence that this behavior is socially harmful. It can leave people less satisfied with their face-to-face interactions. And it can generate feelings of resentment and jealousy. Now, the Journal of Applied Social Psychology has published a new study exploring the reasons for these effects.
segments.cn: 你可能曾和某个在社交场合只顾玩智能手机而忽视你的人待在一起。而且你自己可能也有过这种行为。在 最近的一项调查中,十分之九的受访者表示他们在最近一次社交活动中使用了智能手机。也有证据表明这种 行为对社交有害。它会让人们对面对面互动的满意度降低。而且它还会产生怨恨和嫉妒的情绪。现在,《应 用社会心理学杂志》发表了一项新研究,探讨了产生这些影响的原因。

segments.en: The study included 128 mostly female student participants. The participants watched a three-minute animation in which two cartoon figures interacted and engaged in a conversation. The conversation couldn't be heard but could be detected through mouth movements. Participants had to imagine themselves as the closest figure in the video and then make judgments about the conversations and how they felt about their conversation partners.
segments.cn: 这项研究包括128名参与者,其中大多数是女学生。参与者观看了一段三分钟的动画,画面中两个卡通人物进 行互动并交谈。谈话内容听不到,但可以通过嘴部动作察觉到。参与者必须把自己想象成视频中较近的那个 人物,然后对谈话以及他们对谈话伙伴的感受做出判断。

segments.en: In one version of the experiment, the phone of the participants' conversation partner remained unused on the table throughout the conversation. In another version, their partner's attention was quickly drawn to something on their phone and they spent the rest of the time interacting with their phone. A third version involved the participants' partner alternating between periods of interaction with their phone and periods where they ignored their phone. If you've experienced a similar situation, you probably won't be surprised by the results of the experiments.
segments.cn: 在实验的一个版本中,参与者的谈话伙伴的手机在整个谈话过程中一直放在桌上未使用。在另一个版本中, 他们的伙伴的注意力很快被手机上的某些内容吸引,并在剩余时间里一直在玩手机。第三个版本涉及参与者 的伙伴在玩手机和不理会手机之间交替进行。如果你经历过类似的情况,你可能不会对实验结果感到惊讶。

segments.en: The participants had a negative view of phone use during social interactions. The more it was present, the worse they considered both the quality of the interaction and the quality of the relationship.
segments.cn: 参与者对社交互动期间使用手机持负面看法。手机使用越多,他们就越认为互动质量和关系质量都更差。

segments.en: The researchers believed that focusing on one's phone instead of the person one is with has this effect because it's seen as a form of social exclusion. They assert that the behavior is analogous to when people have no choice but to eat alone in the school cafeteria. The twist is that this exclusion occurs while sharing a physical encounter and having a conversation. Researchers found that the behavior had adverse effects on participants' sense of belonging, need for meaning and self-esteem.
segments.cn: 研究人员认为,专注于自己的手机而不是关注同伴之所以会产生这种影响,是因为它被视为一种社交排斥的 形式。他们断言,这种行为类似于人们别无选择只能独自在学校食堂吃饭的情况。不同的是,这种排斥发生 在共享一次面对面接触并进行谈话的过程中。研究人员发现,这种行为对参与者的归属感、意义需求和自尊 心产生了不利影响。

segments.en: These negative effects are similar to those caused by traditional forms of social exclusion. The new findings are important because they elaborate our understanding of a subtle but common aspect of our daily experience. This common behavior can create vicious cycles of detachment even as we try to connect with others.
segments.cn: 这些负面影响与传统形式的社交排斥造成的影响相似。这些新发现很重要,因为它们完善了我们对日常经历 中一个微妙但常见方面的理解。这种常见行为可能会造成疏离的恶性循环,即使我们试图与他人建立联系。

segments.en: More and more people travel for a variety of reasons. Many are tourists, but many venture forth on personal or professional business. Whatever the reason for traveling, a common complaint of travelers is the impersonal accommodations they find. After spending five consecutive nights in five similar hotels, the business traveler may find it difficult to remember what happened from day to day, or even what towns were visited, and the tourist may get the mistaken impression that all cities are pretty much the same, at least as far as decoration, food and service are concerned.
segments.cn: 越来越多的人因各种原因而旅行。许多人是游客,但也有许多人是为个人或职业事务而出行。无论旅行的原 因是什么,旅行者的一个普遍抱怨是他们所遇到的缺乏个性化的住宿。在连续五个晚上入住五家相似的酒店 后,商务旅行者可能会发现很难记起每天发生了什么,甚至记不清访问了哪些城镇,而游客可能会错误地认为 所有城市都大同小异,至少在装修、食物和服务方面是如此。

segments.en: To combat this sense of impersonal sameness, travelers are taking advantage of in-home hospitality or Bed and Breakfast arrangements. B&Bs, I mean, Bed and Breakfast arrangements are private homes which offer lodging and breakfast in a very personalized, friendly setting. For decades, B&Bs have been the classic way to visit Europe, especially the British Isles. And in fact, they are not really a new idea in America. The tradition dates back to colonial times when inns were few and far between, and the weary traveler had to depend on the kindness of strangers for a meal and a bed. But the revival of B&Bs as desirable accommodations is a fairly recent phenomenon.
segments.cn: 为了对抗这种缺乏个性的雷同感,旅行者正在利用家庭住宿或床位加早餐的安排。B&B,我是说,床位加早餐 安排是私人住宅,在非常个性化、友好的环境中提供住宿和早餐。几十年来,B&B一直是游览欧洲尤其是不 列颠群岛的经典方式。事实上,它们在美国并不是真正的新鲜事物。这一传统可以追溯到殖民时期,当时旅 店稀少,疲惫的旅行者不得不依靠陌生人的善意来获得一顿饭和一张床。但B&B作为理想住宿方式的复兴 是相当近期的现象。

segments.en: If the idea of operating a B&B arouses your interest, there are several factors to consider before plunging into this business. The first consideration is your property, not only the building itself, but the location. If you live near a famous historical site or in a popular destination, such as New York City or Washington, D.C., your home can be fairly simple, yet still do well as a B&B. On the other hand, if your home is architecturally unique or has facilities for the traveler, such as a private entrance, private bath or swimming pool, people may be willing to go some distance to reach you. Another important factor is the lifestyle of you and your family. You must take into account whether all members of the family truly enjoy visitors, want to repeatedly discuss local sites and activities, and have the time and energy to handle the additional cooking, cleaning, laundry and the bookkeeping involved. The final consideration is a financial one, potential B&B hosts must be realistic about opportunities for income. While B&Bs usually have low initial costs, experts estimate it would take at least five rooms rented regularly for the host to earn a living from B&B.
segments.cn: 如果经营B&B的想法引起了你的兴趣,在投身这项业务之前有几个因素需要考虑。首先要考虑的是你的房 产,不仅是建筑本身,还有位置。如果你住在著名历史遗迹附近或热门目的地,如纽约市或华盛顿特区,你的房 子可以相当简单,但仍然可以作为B&B经营得很好。另一方面,如果你的房子在建筑上独具特色或为旅行者 提供便利设施,如独立入口、独立浴室或游泳池,人们可能愿意走一段距离来找你。另一个重要因素是你和 你家人的生活方式。你必须考虑家庭所有成员是否真正喜欢访客,愿意反复讨论当地景点和活动,并有时间 和精力处理额外的烹饪、清洁、洗衣和记账工作。最后要考虑的是财务问题,潜在的B&B房东必须对收入 机会有现实的认识。虽然B&B通常初始成本较低,但专家估计至少需要五个房间定期出租,房东才能靠B&B 谋生。

writing.modelEssay:
It is believed that teachers can exert a profound influence on their students' academic pursuit and personal
development. Having spent years in classrooms, I firmly agree that a dedicated teacher shapes not only what
we learn but also who we become.
On the one hand, teachers guide our academic growth. My high-school chemistry teacher, Mr. Li, turned a
subject I once dreaded into my favourite one. By designing vivid experiments and patiently answering my
endless questions, he inspired me to pursue science and eventually major in it at university. On the other hand,
teachers mould our character. Through his fairness and honesty, Mr. Li taught me to value integrity over easy
shortcuts, a lesson that still steers my decisions today.
In conclusion, a good teacher enlightens the mind and cultivates the heart at the same time. Their influence,
though quiet and gradual, reaches far beyond examinations and often lasts a whole lifetime.

人们普遍认为，教师能对学生的学业追求和人格发展产生深远的影响。在课堂里度过多年之后，我坚定地
赞同这一点：一位敬业的老师塑造的，不仅是我们学到了什么，更是我们成为了什么样的人。
一方面，教师引领我们的学业成长。我高中的化学老师李老师，把一门我曾经害怕的学科变成了我的最
爱。他设计生动的实验，耐心回答我层出不穷的问题，激励我去追求科学，最终让我在大学里选择了它作
为专业。另一方面，教师塑造我们的品格。凭借他的公正与诚实，李老师教会我看重正直、不走投机取巧
的捷径——这个道理至今仍在指引我的抉择。
总之，一位好老师同时启迪头脑、滋养心灵。他们的影响虽然安静而渐进，却远远超越考试，往往伴随人
的一生。

translation.source: 中华民族崇尚自强自立的精神，这一精神深植于中国文化之中，是民族生存与发展的重要支撑。改革开放以来，中国在自强自立的征程上，持续加大科研投入，在信息技术、人工智能、航天工程等领域不断取得新突破。 5G 网络覆盖全国，远程医疗发展迅速，电子支付的使用全球领先，嫦娥探月工程展现了航天领域引人注目的发展。自强自主精神成为推动国家现代化进程的强大动力，激励着中国人民为实现民族复兴  (rejuvenation) 的中国梦不断奋进。
translation.reference: The Chinese nation values the spirit of self-reliance and self-improvement, which is deeply rooted in Chinese culture and serves as a vital support for the survival and development of the nation. Since the reform and opening-up, China has continued to increase its investment in scientific research on its journey toward self-reliance, and has kept making new breakthroughs in such fields as information technology, artificial intelligence and aerospace engineering. For example, 5G networks now cover the whole country, telemedicine is developing rapidly, and electronic payment is used more widely than anywhere else in the world; the Chang'e lunar exploration program also demonstrates remarkable progress in China's aerospace field. B.en: Think about that relationship you held on to even after it had run its course or the job you stayed in despite your boss making you miserable. Many of us try to hold onto the last ray of hope, thinking we can make it work, whatever "it" is. B.cn: 想想那段你即使在它已经走到尽头后仍坚持的关系,或者那份尽管老板让你痛苦不堪却仍留守的工作。 我们中的许多人试图抓住最后一线希望,认为我们可以让它成功,无论"它"是什么。虽然坚持不懈通常是 一种优秀的品质,但它也可能使你过度投资于一件不再明智的事情。

C.en: As an executive coach, I work with numerous passionate and hard-working leaders who don't want to "quit". But the smartest leaders learn to discern the difference between quitting too soon and holding onto something that they shouldn't.

Q.en: Undeniably, perseverance can help us succeed. But for your well-being, it's important to learn how to distinguish quitting too soon and clinging to a losing course of action. While letting go can be difficult, it will free up your time, energy, and mental space to imagine new possibilities and pursue new opportunities.
Q.cn: 不可否认,坚持不懈可以帮助我们成功。但为了你的幸福,学会如何区分过早放弃和坚持失败的行动方针 是很重要的。虽然放手可能很难,但它会释放你的时间、精力和心理空间,让你想象新的可能性并追求新 的机会。

paragraphs.en: As interdependent beings we cannot thrive independent of others. We like to work with people who are like- minded, with whom we share a common interest, or who also believe in a cause we are serious about. This is evident in how we have organized ourselves into various collective groups such as nations, regions, communities, organizations, and families.
paragraphs.cn: 作为相互依存的存在，我们无法独立于他人而兴旺发展。我们喜欢与志同道合的人共事，与我们有共同兴 趣的人共事，或者与同样相信我们所认真对待的事业的人共事。这在我们如何将自己组织成各种集体群体 中表现得很明显，如国家、地区、社区、组织和家庭。

paragraphs.en: Does the group you belong to have a strong collective consciousness or shared beliefs? Is there interdependence among its members? Do you consider this group a significant part of your existence? If your answers are affirmative, then you are experiencing a micro version of solidarity.
paragraphs.cn: 你所属的群体是否有强烈的集体意识或共同信念？其成员之间是否存在相互依存关系？你是否认为这个群 体是你存在的重要组成部分？如果你的答案是肯定的，那么你正在经历团结的微缩版本。

paragraphs.en: What is solidarity? Its simplest definition in the dictionary is: "... a unifying opinion, feeling, purpose or interest among a group of people."
paragraphs.cn: 什么是团结？字典中对它最简单的定义是："……一群人之间统一的观点、感受、目的或利益。"

paragraphs.en: In this increasingly diverse society we live in, solidarity takes on a complex and multifaceted character as it forms bonds of interdependence among unique individuals living in a fast-changing environment and working within a complex division of labor.
paragraphs.cn: 在我们生活的这个日益多元化的社会中，团结呈现出复杂和多面的特征，因为它在生活于快速变化的环境 中并在复杂的劳动分工中工作的独特个体之间形成相互依存的纽带。

paragraphs.en: One facet of solidarity fits well with the principles of communitarianism (社 群 主 义). In this setting, individuals give up their own interests to serve the common good. However, its strict adherence to social cohesiveness and exclusiveness restricts expression and practice of individual differences and preferences. Consequently, individuality and autonomy is sacrificed to maintain the unity of the group.
paragraphs.cn: 团结的一个方面与社群主义的原则非常契合。在这种情况下，个人放弃自己的利益来服务于共同利益。然 而，它对社会凝聚力和排他性的严格遵守限制了个体差异和偏好的表达和实践。因此，个性和自主性被牺 牲以维护群体的团结。

paragraphs.en: Solidarity is also viewed as a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism and freedom of choice. It goes against the liberal idea of unrestricted individuals who see society as a hindrance to their freedom to make choices and to act according to what is good for them regardless of how these will affect others.
paragraphs.cn: 团结也被视为对过度强调个人主义和选择自由的一种反应。它反对自由主义关于不受限制的个人的观念， 这些个人将社会视为阻碍他们自由做出选择和根据对自己有利的事情行事的障碍，而不管这些会如何影响 他人。

paragraphs.en: But despite its many facets, social theorists have viewed solidarity as a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society. They believe that for human society to survive as it becomes more diverse, more new bonds need to be formed based on the differences. In the light of this, they regard a genuine solidarity as more than just shallow relationships based on common interests. Solidarity is not just a product of strategic calculations of how much it will benefit the self. It is not an exclusive class founded on the you-and-me-against- the-world principle. Rather, it is inclusive and is not forced. Acting out of solidarity means supporting and standing up for each other - in recognition that one's fate is in the fate of the other. It is a bond characterized by cooperative practices and strengthened by the concern for the well-being of others or the common good. It fights for the protection of human dignity and listens to and acts on the cries of the most vulnerable.
paragraphs.cn: 但尽管团结有许多方面，社会理论家将团结视为给社会带来秩序和进步的关键因素。他们认为，随着人类 社会变得更加多元化，要使其生存下去，就需要基于差异形成更多新的纽带。鉴于此，他们认为真正的团 结不仅仅是基于共同利益的肤浅关系。团结不仅仅是关于它将给自我带来多少利益的战略计算的产物。它 不是建立在你我对抗世界原则基础上的排他性阶层。相反，它是包容性的，不是强制的。出于团结而行动 意味着相互支持和挺身而出——认识到一个人的命运在于另一个人的命运之中。这是一种以合作实践为特 征、以对他人福祉或共同利益的关注而得到加强的纽带。它为保护人类尊严而战，倾听并回应最脆弱者的 呼声。

paragraphs.en: People who repeatedly give unwanted advice can be well-meaning and genuinely want to help. Others might do this out of a sense of self-worth around the ability to influence others. One study found that people with a high tendency to seek power were more likely to give advice than those with an opposite tendency.
paragraphs.cn: 反复提供不请自来的建议的人可能出于好意,真心想要帮忙。另一些人这样做可能是出于一种围绕影响他人 能力的自我价值感。一项研究发现,权力寻求倾向高的人比倾向相反的人更容易给出建议。

paragraphs.en: Under the guise (外表) of unselfishness, people may be driven to give you unwanted advice because it makes them feel powerful or in control. They may not be fully aware of this drive, however.
paragraphs.cn: 在无私的外表下,人们可能被驱使给你提供不想要的建议,因为这让他们感到强大或能够掌控。然而,他们可 能并未完全意识到这种驱动力。

paragraphs.en: These people may also display a problematic degree of emotional vulnerability, becoming upset very quickly, and taking a long time to calm down. It is possible that their emotions were only validated in childhood when they were at their loudest, encouraging them to adopt responses to discomfort that are excessive in most situations.
paragraphs.cn: 这些人还可能表现出问题性的情绪脆弱程度,很快变得心烦意乱,需要很长时间才能平静下来。有可能他们 的情绪在童年时期只有在最大声时才得到认可,这促使他们采用在大多数情况下都过度的不适应对方式。

paragraphs.en: When someone is giving advice in order to make themselves feel more powerful, there is underlying anxiety to their behavior that recipients of the advice tend to notice. It can be tempting in this situation to react harshly to the advice giver and to accuse them of being manipulative, but this approach might produce an undesired result.
paragraphs.cn: 当某人为了让自己感觉更强大而给出建议时,他们的行为背后有焦虑,建议的接受者往往会注意到这一点。 在这种情况下,对建议给予者做出严厉反应并指责他们具有操纵性可能很诱人,但这种方法可能会产生不希 望的结果。

paragraphs.en: If the act of giving advice is contributing actively to someone's feelings of self-worth, an outright (直率的) rejection may be perceived as a threat, activating their fight-or-flight response, possibly causing them to double down on their validation-seeking behavior, or leading to a larger conflict.
paragraphs.cn: outright( 直率的 ) rejection may be perceived as a threat, activating their fight-or-flight response, possibly 如果给出建议的行为正在积极促成某人的自我价值感,直率的拒绝可能被视为一种威胁,激活他们的战斗或 逃跑反应,可能导致他们加倍寻求认可的行为,或导致更大的冲突。

paragraphs.en: The key is to validate without over-identifying. You can let them know that you have heard them and appreciate where they are coming from without taking on the potentially damaging narrative that you could not have gotten by without their help. You had better say something like, "Thanks for the idea. I have my own plan for handling this, but I really appreciate your perspective and will take it into consideration. Can I let you know when I need help in the future?"
paragraphs.cn: 关键是要认可但不要过度认同。你可以让他们知道你听到了他们的意见,理解他们的出发点,而不必接受那 种可能有害的叙事,即没有他们的帮助你就无法做到。你最好说些类似这样的话:'感谢你的想法。我有自己 处理这件事的计划,但我真的很感激你的观点,会将它纳入考虑。将来我需要帮助时可以告诉你吗?'

paragraphs.en: If you have trouble setting boundaries tactfully, prioritize working on your own ability to self-regulate. As uncomfortable as it may make you continuously receiving unwanted advice, if you can respond with compassion, the situation will likely diffuse much faster.
paragraphs.cn: 如果你在巧妙地设定界限方面有困难,优先致力于提高自己的自我调节能力。尽管持续接受可能令人不舒 服,但如果你能以同情心回应,情况可能会更快缓和。

paragraphs.en: Though it is usually not the intended outcome of giving unsolicited advice, many who receive it often feel stressed, offended, or simply annoyed by unwanted suggestions. Setting a boundary in this regard, if you feel you need one, is perfectly reasonable and something that can bring you increased emotional safety.
paragraphs.cn: 尽管这通常不是主动提供建议的预期结果,但许多接受建议的人常常因不想要的建议而感到压力、被冒犯或 只是感到恼火。在这方面设定界限,如果你觉得需要,是完全合理的,也是能给你带来更多情感安全的事情。

paragraphs.en: It is best to set boundaries in a way that takes into account the individual's underlying reasons for doing what they are doing to avoid unnecessary conflict and more stress.
paragraphs.cn: 最好以考虑到个人做事的潜在原因的方式设定界限,以避免不必要的冲突和更多压力。

segments.speaker: W
segments.en: Hi, Tony, today we're talking about how managers can get along better with young people at work. We often hear young people today have a poor work ethic. That's not really justified though, is it?
segments.cn: 嗨,Tony,今天我们要谈谈管理者如何更好地与工作中的年轻人相处。我们经常听到说如今的年轻人缺乏 职业道德。不过这其实并不合理,对吧?

segments.speaker: M
segments.en: Not really. In reality, young people of this age group are as varied and multifaceted as any other generation.
segments.cn: 确实不合理。实际上,这个年龄段的年轻人和其他任何一代人一样多样化和多面化。

segments.speaker: W
segments.en: Yeah, but if you are struggling to work with young people in your workspace, what can you do?
segments.cn: 是的,但如果你在工作场所与年轻人合作时遇到困难,你能做些什么呢?

segments.speaker: M
segments.en: Well, it's essential to connect with them to learn about their values. It's also really important to recognize the way young people want to balance their work life with their personal life.
segments.cn: 嗯,与他们建立联系以了解他们的价值观是非常重要的。同样非常重要的是要认识到年轻人希望平衡工 作生活和个人生活的方式。

segments.speaker: W
segments.en: So they generally don't want to defer happiness in return for career advancement?
segments.cn: 所以他们通常不愿意为了职业晋升而推迟幸福?

segments.speaker: M
segments.en: Absolutely. They are not willing to sacrifice their personal lives for their work lives and this leads people to equate that with an unwillingness to work hard.
segments.cn: 完全正确。他们不愿意为了工作生活而牺牲个人生活,这导致人们将其等同于不愿意努力工作。

segments.speaker: W
segments.en: Right. But that couldn't be further from the truth, could it?
segments.cn: 对。但这与事实相去甚远,不是吗?

segments.speaker: M
segments.en: Young people will work extremely hard during their defined work hours, but they expect to have their time off, like weekends and nights free from work.
segments.cn: 年轻人会在规定的工作时间内极其努力地工作,但他们期望拥有自己的休息时间,比如周末和晚上不受工 作打扰。

segments.speaker: W
segments.en: So how should managers go about assessing young people's productivity?
segments.cn: 那么管理者应该如何评估年轻人的生产力呢?

segments.speaker: M
segments.en: Generally, young people believe their productivity should not be measured by the number of hours they work, since someone can work for eight hours and accomplish next to nothing of significance for the company. Instead, young people measure their productivity levels by the quality of the work they perform.
segments.cn: 一般来说,年轻人认为他们的生产力不应该用工作时长来衡量,因为有人可以工作八小时却几乎没为公司 完成任何有意义的事情。相反,年轻人通过他们所完成工作的质量来衡量自己的生产力水平。

segments.speaker: W
segments.en: But we often hear that young people want to feel more than just being a part of a big machine. Such a perspective can be hard to discredit, can't it?
segments.cn: 但我们经常听到年轻人想要感觉自己不只是大机器中的一部分。这样的观点很难被否定,对吧?

segments.speaker: M
segments.en: It's important to legitimize their work. Young workers want to work on projects that matter to themselves, the company or the world at large. They must feel the need to stay working at a company whose values align with their own.
segments.cn: 使他们的工作合理化是很重要的。年轻员工想要从事对自己、对公司或对整个世界都重要的项目。他 们必须感到有必要继续在一家价值观与自己相符的公司工作。

segments.speaker: W
segments.en: Thanks for your advice.
segments.cn: 谢谢你的建议。

segments.en: Many restaurants are trying to persuade customers to eat more sustainably, moving away from environmentally unfriendly meat towards greener dishes. Although it sounds counter-intuitive, restaurants which include specific vegetarian sections on their menus may be unintentionally encouraging customers to eat meat, a new study suggests.
segments.cn: 许多餐厅正试图说服顾客更可持续地饮食，从对环境不友好的肉类转向更环保的菜肴。一项新研究表明， 尽管听起来有违直觉，但在菜单上设置专门素食区的餐厅可能会无意中鼓励顾客吃肉。

segments.en: Behavioral scientist Linda Bacon, one of the study's authors, said, "Restaurants can have a positive impact on the environment by encouraging their customers to choose more plant-based food and less meat. However, our findings suggest that while certain restaurant menu designs can encourage some consumers to make pro-environmental food choices, they can have the opposite effect on others." The study involved 750 people, half of whom frequently ate vegetarian food and half of whom rarely ate it. No vegetarians were included. They were given different menus and asked to choose a meal as if they were eating out with friends. Placing vegetarian dishes in a separate section did not have a significant effect on the choices made by infrequent vegetarian food eaters. But it did have a notable effect on the frequent eaters, lowering their chance of picking a vegetarian option by 65%. The researchers also discovered that presenting a vegetarian dish as the chef's recommendation, or including a more appealing description of a non-meat meal, leads to a greater proportion of infrequent vegetarian eaters choosing a vegetarian option. But again, these altered menu designs backfired with those who ate vegetarian food more frequently, leading them to be less likely to choose a vegetarian dish.
segments.cn: 该研究的作者之一、行为科学家Linda Bacon说："餐厅可以通过鼓励顾客选择更多植物性食物和更少肉类 来对环境产生积极影响。然而,我们的研究结果表明,虽然某些餐厅菜单设计可以鼓励一些消费者做出有利 于环境的食物选择,但它们可能对其他人产生相反的效果。"这项研究涉及750人,其中一半人经常吃素食,另 一半人很少吃素食。研究不包括素食主义者。他们拿到不同的菜单,并被要求选择一餐,就像和朋友外出就 餐一样。将素食菜肴放在单独的区域对不常吃素食者的选择没有显著影响。但它确实对常吃素食者产生了 显著影响,使他们选择素食选项的可能性降低了65%。研究人员还发现,将素食菜肴作为厨师推荐呈现,或加 入对非肉类餐食更具吸引力的描述,会导致更大比例的不常吃素食者选择素食选项。但这些改变的菜单设计 再次对那些更频繁吃素食的人适得其反,导致他们不太可能选择素食菜肴。

segments.en: Nottingham Trent University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences have been trying to find a way to prevent deadly outdoor air pollution from penetrating indoors. They found that if pollution is frozen to around –18 ℃  in a condensing tube, the particles gather together and fall to the bottom, allowing fresh, clean air to pass through. Their method was able to remove 99% of pollutants. It is hoped that the work could pave the way for simple modification of air conditioning units so that they can also clean polluted indoor air.
segments.cn: Nottingham Trent University和中国科学院一直在尝试寻找一种方法来防止致命的室外空气污染渗透到 室内。他们发现，如果在冷凝管中将污染物冷冻到约–18℃，颗粒物会聚集在一起并沉降到底部，从而让 新鲜、洁净的空气通过。他们的方法能够去除99%的污染物。希望这项工作能够为空调设备的简单改造铺 平道路，使其也能清洁受污染的室内空气。

segments.en: Outdoor air pollution in cities is a global problem, whether it be haze plaguing Calcutta or poor air impacting the health of children in London schools. While there are some existing technologies to purify indoor air, they can be inefficient, expensive or produce harmful by-products. When outdoor air quality is poor, people tend to spend even more time indoors. But outdoor pollution also leads to indoor pollution, and people still suffer. It is estimated that pollution is linked to over 40,000 early deaths in Britain each year. Professor Gang Pan of the Chinese Academy of Sciences said, "We have shown in our experiments that simply by circulating polluted air through a small freezing chamber, we can remove most of the fine particles and gas pollutants. Our study makes it possible to add an air cleaner option to household appliances in areas which might experience extremely poor air conditions. By controlling indoor air pollution and improving air quality in this way, this work could be greatly beneficial to public health."
segments.cn: 城市室外空气污染是一个全球性问题，无论是困扰Calcutta的雾霾还是影响伦敦学校儿童健康的恶劣空 气。虽然现有一些净化室内空气的技术，但它们可能效率低下、成本高昂或产生有害副产品。当室外空气 质量差时，人们往往会在室内待更长时间。但室外污染也会导致室内污染，人们仍然会受到影响。据估 计，英国每年有超过40,000例早死与污染有关。中国科学院的潘刚教授说："我们在实验中证明，仅仅通 过让受污染的空气循环通过一个小型冷冻室，我们就能去除大部分细颗粒物和气体污染物。我们的研究使 得在可能经历极端恶劣空气条件的地区，为家用电器增加空气净化功能成为可能。通过以这种方式控制室 内空气污染和改善空气质量，这项工作可能对公共健康大有裨益。

segments.en: Research recently carried out by my team suggests that fish may be self-aware. A certain species of fish recently passed the well-known mirror test.
segments.cn: 我的团队最近进行的研究表明，鱼类可能具有自我意识。某种鱼类最近通过了著名的镜子测试。

segments.en: This is a test that demonstrates self-recognition in animals. Only a few animals, such as humans, apes, dolphins and some birds, can recognize themselves in a mirror. And only these animals, capable of self- recognition, will attempt to remove marks placed on their skin after noticing them in the reflection. This ability suggests a level of higher intelligence and awareness. This is not shown by children until around 18 months. Until now, no fish has demonstrated the ability. But our experiments show the fish in question will scrape up against hard surfaces to remove marks placed on its body by our researchers after viewing itself in a mirror. The behaviors we observe leave little doubt that this fish behaviorally fulfills all criteria of the mirror test as originally laid out. The fish in our study never attempted to remove the marks when no mirror was present or when the marks were just placed on the mirror. Unmarked fish also did not attempt to remove marks from themselves when interacting with a marked fish on the other side of a window. These results show either that fish are self-aware or that the mirror test, which is considered to be the gold standard test used to denote higher intelligence, may be flawed.
segments.cn: 这是一项证明动物自我识别能力的测试。只有少数动物，如人类、猿类、海豚和某些鸟类，能够在镜子中 识别自己。而且只有这些具备自我识别能力的动物，在镜子中注意到标记后，才会试图去除放置在其皮肤 上的标记。这种能力表明了更高水平的智力和意识。人类儿童直到大约18个月大时才表现出这种能力。到 目前为止，还没有鱼类展现出这种能力。但我们的实验表明，该鱼类在镜子中看到自己后，会在坚硬表面 上摩擦，以去除研究人员在其身上放置的标记。我们观察到的行为几乎毫无疑问地表明，这种鱼在行为上 完全符合最初制定的镜子测试的所有标准。在我们的研究中，当没有镜子存在时，或者当标记只是放在镜 子上时,该鱼从未试图去除标记。当未标记的鱼与窗户另一边的已标记鱼互动时，也不会试图去除自己身上 的标记。这些结果表明，要么鱼类具有自我意识，要么被认为是用于表示更高智力的黄金标准测试的镜子 测试可能存在缺陷。

segments.en: What is less clear is whether these behaviors should be considered as evidence that fish are self- aware, even though in the past these same behaviors have been interpreted as self-awareness in so many other animals. Depending on your position, you might reject the interpretation that these behaviors in a fish satisfy passing the test at all. But on what objective basis can you do this when the behaviors they show are so functionally similar to those of other species that have passed the test?
segments.cn: 不太清楚的是，这些行为是否应被视为鱼类具有自我意识的证据，尽管过去这些相同的行为在许多其他动 物身上被解释为自我意识。根据你的立场，你可能会拒绝接受鱼类的这些行为满足通过测试的解释。但 是，当它们表现出的行为与其他通过测试的物种在功能上如此相似时，你能在什么客观基础上这样做呢？

segments.en: Results from our research raise more questions than answers. What if self-awareness develops like an onion, building layer upon layer rather than appearing all at once? Perhaps in order to explore self- awareness further, we should stop looking at responses to the mirror as a decisive test. Only with a richer theory of the self and a larger test battery will we be able to determine all of the various levels of self-awareness, including where exactly fish fit in.
segments.cn: 我们的研究结果引发的问题多于答案。如果自我意识像洋葱一样发展，一层层地累积而不是一次性出现， 会怎样？也许为了进一步探索自我意识，我们应该停止将对镜子的反应视为决定性测试。只有拥有更丰 富的自我理论和更大规模的测试组合，我们才能确定自我意识的各个不同层次，包括鱼类究竟处于什么 位置。

segments.en: Reading with a young child is important. But does it matter whether you read from an electronic book or traditional print? As any parent knows, small children are generally keen on screens. So the finding from a new study that very young children enjoy electronic books more than printed picture books may not come as a huge surprise — but the following additional findings might: both parents and children behaved differently when reading electronic versus printed picture books. And the children who read the electronic books learned more.
segments.cn: 与幼儿一起阅读很重要。但从电子书还是传统纸质书阅读是否有区别？正如任何父母所知，小孩子通常对 屏幕很感兴趣。因此，一项新研究发现幼儿比起纸质图画书更喜欢电子书，这可能不会让人感到特别惊讶 ——但以下额外的发现可能会：父母和孩子在阅读电子图画书与纸质图画书时的行为都有所不同。而且阅 读电子书的孩子学到了更多。

segments.en: Previous studies of young children have suggested that electronic books, which incorporate extra features such as dictionaries and images that depict story events, may have advantages over print. In fact, multiple studies have found that electronic books support story comprehension and vocabulary gains beyond what is provided by printed books. But there's also work suggesting that children sometimes invest less mental effort in learning from electronic books, and that parents talk less about content when sharing such books.
segments.cn: 以往对幼儿的研究表明，包含额外功能（如词典和描绘故事情节的图像）的电子书可能比纸质书更有优 势。事实上，多项研究发现，电子书对故事理解和词汇量增长的支持超过了纸质书所能提供的。但也有研 究表明，儿童有时在从电子书学习时投入的心理努力较少，而且父母在分享这类书籍时对内容的讨论也 较少。

segments.en: The study we're looking at today aims to give us a better understanding of how good electronic books are for young children. For this study, researchers videoed children aged 17 to 26 months reading with one of their parents. Each parent-child pair was randomly assigned to read either two educational electronic books or two printed books with the same content. While the parent read the words in the printed books aloud, the electronic books had audio of voice actors reading the text.
segments.cn: 我们今天关注的这项研究旨在让我们更好地了解电子书对幼儿有多好。在这项研究中，研究人员录制了17 至26个月大的儿童与其父母之一一起阅读的视频。每对亲子被随机分配阅读两本教育性电子书或两本内容 相同的纸质书。父母在朗读纸质书中的文字时，电子书则有配音演员朗读文本的音频。

segments.en: The researchers found that parents who read the printed books pointed more frequently to pages than parents who read the electronic books. But the opposite was true for the children. Children who read the electronic books also commented more on the content and learned more new words than the children who read printed books.
segments.cn: 研究人员发现，阅读纸质书的父母指向书页的频率高于阅读电子书的父母。但对于孩子来说情况正好相 反。阅读电子书的孩子对内容的评论也更多，学到的新词汇也比阅读纸质书的孩子更多。

segments.en: This greater learning is ascribed to greater engagement with the electronic books. It's important to note that the electronic books in the study were simple. While they included background music, animation and sound effects, there were no other extra features.
segments.cn: 这种更大的学习成效归因于对电子书更高的参与度。值得注意的是，研究中的电子书很简单。虽然它们包 含背景音乐、动画和音效，但没有其他额外功能。

segments.en: It's also important to note that there's research on older children, finding that electronic books don't always bolster learning. Parents and educators need to beware. Extra features in electronic books may increase children's participation with them; however, if these features don't draw attention to the educational content, they may not serve as a supportive feature.
segments.cn: 同样重要的是要注意，有关于年龄较大儿童的研究发现，电子书并不总是促进学习。父母和教育工作者需 要警惕。电子书中的额外功能可能会增加儿童对它们的参与；然而，如果这些功能没有将注意力引向教育 内容，它们可能不会起到支持作用。

segments.en: Let me be honest with you. If you're living your life full of regrets, you're wasting your time. Why would you go through life regretting the very decisions that made you who you are today? There are plenty of unfavorable decisions we've made, but does that mean we should regret them? No!
segments.cn: 让我对你坦诚相待。如果你的生活充满悔恨，那你就是在浪费时间。你为什么要在人生中悔恨那些造就了 今天的你的决定呢?我们确实做过许多不利的决定,但这是否意味着我们应该后悔它们?不!

segments.en: I've had many moments where I sit and think about all the things I wish I could have done differently. However, just because things could be different, it doesn't necessarily mean they would be better. You don't have to continually be thinking of all your past decisions and whether or not you made the right one. You can't go back and change anything, so what's the point in worrying about it?
segments.cn: 我曾有许多时刻坐下来思考所有我希望能做得不同的事情。然而,仅仅因为事情可能会不同,并不一定意味 着它们会更好。你不必不断地思考你过去所有的决定以及你是否做出了正确的选择。你无法回去改变任何 事情,所以为此担忧有什么意义呢?

segments.en: Every single decision you've ever made, positive or negative, has made you the person you are today. We want to go back and change parts of our past, but what would be the benefit of that? We would have lost the valuable knowledge from the lessons we learned.
segments.cn: 你曾经做过的每一个决定,无论积极还是消极,都造就了今天的你。我们想回去改变过去的某些部分,但那样 做有什么好处呢?我们会失去从所学教训中获得的宝贵知识。

segments.en: There are reasons you make the choices you do, and that tells us about who you are. So when it comes to any decision in life, be unapologetically yourself. Because at the end of the day, it was you who made that decision.
segments.cn: 你做出选择是有原因的,这说明了你是什么样的人。所以当涉及人生中的任何决定时,要毫无歉意地做你自 己。因为归根结底,是你做出了那个决定。

segments.en: With less time spent focused on regrets, you'll finally have time to focus on the more essential things in life. In any situation, you grow more as a person with every decision you make. Life is full of lessons to learn, so we can't let regret stop us from moving forward.
segments.cn: 少花时间关注悔恨,你终于有时间专注于生活中更重要的事情。在任何情况下,你做出的每个决定都会让你 更加成长。生活充满了要学习的教训,所以我们不能让悔恨阻止我们前进。

segments.en: We don't know if we've made the right or wrong choice until after it's already been made, so it can be easy to start regretting your decision. But if the decision has already been made, what's the purpose of dwelling on it? There isn't one. All you can do is move forward. You can't let yourself sit there and worry about every past choice. We aren't all perfect.
segments.cn: 我们不知道自己是否做出了正确或错误的选择,直到决定已经做出之后,所以很容易开始后悔你的决定。但 如果决定已经做出,纠结于此有什么目的呢?没有。你所能做的就是向前看。你不能让自己坐在那里为每一 个过去的选择而担忧。我们都不是完美的。

segments.en: Whenever you make a decision, there will always be a possibility for regret later, but that's how life is supposed to be. You will make poor decisions in life — we all do — but it's what you do with the lessons learned that matters.
segments.cn: 每当你做出决定时,以后总会有后悔的可能性,但这就是生活本该如此。你会在生活中做出糟糕的决定—— 我们都会——但重要的是你如何运用所学到的教训。

segments.en: Think about every decision you've ever made. Were they always the best? Of course not. But look at how far you've come since then.
segments.cn: 想想你曾经做过的每一个决定。它们总是最好的吗?当然不是。但看看你从那时起走了多远。

writing.modelEssay:
Living in an increasingly competitive world, college students should better prepare themselves to confront
various challenges. This preparation is no longer optional but essential, for those who wait passively will
inevitably be left behind.
To begin with, students ought to equip themselves with solid knowledge and practical skills rather than merely
chasing high marks. For instance, in today's fierce job market, employers value candidates who can
communicate, cooperate and solve real problems. What is more, developing a resilient mindset matters just as
much. I still remember failing my first internship interview; instead of giving up, I reflected on my
weaknesses, practised repeatedly, and finally secured a position the next semester. That experience taught me
that challenges are conquered by those who keep improving.
Therefore, it is high time that college students stopped drifting and started planning ahead. By strengthening
both our abilities and our willpower, we can turn the pressure of competition into a driving force and stride
confidently into the future.
writing.modelCn:
生活在一个竞争日益激烈的世界里，大学生应当更好地武装自己，去迎接各种挑战。这种准备不再是可有
可无，而是不可或缺的，因为那些被动等待的人终将被甩在后面。
首先，学生应当用扎实的知识和实用的技能武装自己，而不是一味追求高分。例如，在当今竞争激烈的就
业市场，用人单位看重的是能够沟通、协作并解决实际问题的求职者。此外，培养一种坚韧的心态同样重
要。我至今记得第一次实习面试失利；我没有放弃，而是反思自己的不足，反复练习，终于在下个学期争
取到了一个职位。那段经历让我明白：挑战属于那些不断进步的人。
因此，大学生该停止随波逐流、开始提前规划了。通过同时强化我们的能力与意志，我们就能把竞争的压
力转化为前进的动力，自信地大步迈向未来。

translation.source: 节俭  (frugality) 是中华民族的传统美德。在中国古代，生产力低下，先人们深知劳动成果来之不易，因而秉持节俭的理念。到了物质极大丰富的今天，中国人民依然坚持节俭的生活方式，体现了理性消费的生活理念和对劳动的尊重。近年来，中国政府持续加强节约型社会的建设，倡导 " 光盘行动 " ，减少食物浪费，提倡简约低碳的生活方式，推进资源循环利用，反对过度消费。节约型社会的建设有力地推动了中国经济的高质量发展。
translation.reference: Frugality is a traditional virtue of the Chinese nation. In ancient China, productivity was low, and our ancestors knew well that the fruits of labor did not come easily, so they upheld the idea of frugality. Today, when material wealth is abundant, the Chinese people still maintain a frugal lifestyle, reflecting their concept of rational consumption and their respect for labor. In recent years, the Chinese government has been strengthening the building of a resource-conserving society by advocating the "Clear Your Plate" campaign to reduce food waste, promoting a simple and low-carbon lifestyle, advancing the recycling of resources, and opposing excessive consumption. This building of a resource-conserving society has strongly promoted the high-quality development of China's economy.

cloze.passage: It’s best to think of an accent as a distinct, systematic and rule-governed way of speaking. Accent is not a __26__ for dialect, but it’s related. Dialect is an umbrella term for the way a community pronounces words, creates words, and orders words; accent refers to that first part only. Many __27__ presume that there is a single standard way of speaking in each country, with one single standard accent, and that this perceived standard is __28__ the best form of speech, but linguists (语言学家) often point out that the concept of a standard accent is better understood as an ideal rather than a __29__ . In other words, no one speaks “standard English”; rather, it is an imagined way of using language that exists only in grammar and style books. One reason linguists agree there is no one true standard is that, through the years, there have been __30__ supposed standards, depending on time and place. The standard for English in British newsreels (新闻片) from the 1950s, for example, differs greatly from the standard found on American national news broadcasts today. In fact, there has never been a single standard that’s been fully agreed upon — and broadcast outlets across the __31__ have never consistently held to those standards anyway. Even so, this idea of a standard accent is __32__ and many workplace and educational environments perpetuate the idea that accents that __33__ from the current standard are less appropriate, or even inappropriate. Scholars have found that southern US accent features are more accepted in __34__ such as government, law and service-oriented workplaces, but less accepted in the technology sector. The acceptability of nonstandard accents may __35__ with differences in class and culture, with newer or higher prestige industries expecting more standard speech in the workplace.

The History and Meaning of Colored Traffic Lights A) Timed traffic lights are set according to schedules that are supposed to coordinate with peak traffic hours. Cities need to monitor and update signal light time schedules at least every two years to keep these systems effective. In Los Angeles, California, an ambitious project to go a step further and synchronize( 使同步 ) every red light in Los Angeles cost over 400 million dollars. However, none of this would be possible without the traffic light! 定时交通信号灯根据应当与高峰交通时段相协调的时刻表进行设置。城市需要至少每两年监测和更新 信号灯时间安排,以保持这些系统的有效性。在加利福尼亚州洛杉矶,一项更进一步同步洛杉矶每个红灯 的雄心勃勃的项目耗资超过4亿美元。问问这座城市的居民,他们很可能会认为节省道路上的时间非常 值得。如果在全国范围内实施,同步化可以减少10%的交通拥堵和20%的空气污染。拥堵浪费时间、金 钱和生命。大数据可以帮助改善数百万人安全共享道路的方式。然而,如果没有交通信号灯,这一切都不 可能实现! B) The first traffic light was invented in London in the 1860's, but it was hardly recognizable — or effective. match.title: The History and Meaning of Colored Traffic Lights

A.en: Timed traffic lights are set according to schedules that are supposed to coordinate with peak traffic hours. Cities need to monitor and update signal light time schedules at least every two years to keep these systems effective. In Los Angeles, California, an ambitious project to go a step further and synchronize (使同步) every red light in Los Angeles cost over 400 million dollars. Ask a resident of the city and they are likely to agree that saving time on the road is well worth it. If implemented nationwide, synchronization could shave 10% off traffic congestion (堵 塞) and 20% off air pollution. Congestion costs time, money, and lives. Big data can help improve how millions of people safely share the road. However, none of this would be possible without the traffic light!

B.en: The first traffic light was invented in London in the 1860's, but it was hardly recognizable - or effective. It had been adapted from the railroad signal system by a railway manager, John Peak Knight, in 1868. The railroads used red gas lights at night to signal stops and green gas lights during the daytime. Knight installed a similar gas light, semaphore (臂板信号) system near London's Westminster Bridge in December of 1868.

C.en: The life of the first traffic light signal was short-lived. A gas leak caused one of the signal lights to explode on its police officer operator within a month of being installed.

E.en: The United States is a car culture like no other country. Unlike most European cities that started urban planning when horses were high-tech, many cities in the United States were designed around urban sprawl, suburban tracts, and motor cars.

F.en: As traffic and cities grew, so did the race to solve growing traffic problems. The first traffic signals were semaphores. Semaphores are towers with moving arms signaling for traffic to stop or go. They could be manual or automatic. There was no consistent design. V arious models were invented and put into place in cities as the need arose.

statements.text: What a traffic light means is almost the same everywhere despite some variations.
statements.locateEn: Traffic light meaning is fairly consistent across the board with various deviations.
statements.locateCn: 总体来看，红绿灯的含义大体上保持一致，只是存在一些差异。

statements.text: Pedestrian crossings came into being only in the mid-twentieth century.

statements.locateCn: 人行横道甚至直到 1951 年才出现。

statements.text: People raced to address increasing traffic problems along with the expansion of cities and traffic.
statements.locateEn: As traffic and cities grew, so did the race to solve growing traffic problems.
statements.locateCn: 随着交通和城市的扩张，解决日益严重的交通问题的竞赛也愈演愈烈。

statements.text: When the warning yellow light was introduced, driving became safer and traffic accidents reduced.
statements.locateEn: The introduction of the cautionary yellow light helped increase driver safety, decreasing accidents that come from running red lights.
statements.locateCn: 警示性黄灯的引入帮助提高了驾驶者的安全，减少了因闯红灯导致的事故。

statements.text: The signal system on the railroad served as the basis for the first traffic light.
statements.locateEn: It had been adapted from the railroad signal system by a railway manager, John Peak Knight, in 1868.
statements.locateCn: 它是 1868 年由铁路经理 John Peak Knight 仿照铁路信号系统改造而来的。

statements.text: Even though a green light signals "go", attention should be paid to traffic on either side in case some

statements.locateCn: 绿灯表示通行。就这么简单，但最好还是双向都看一下，留意那些可能心不在焉、或者正在 闯灯的对向车辆。

paragraphs.en: Mindfulness has been shown to have a number of meaningful health benefits - it can help reduce anxiety and promote healing in those suffering from chronic illness.
paragraphs.cn: 正念已被证明具有许多重要的健康益处——它可以帮助减少焦虑,并促进慢性疾病患者的康复。

paragraphs.en: The practice is based on an insight first described in ancient Buddhist texts that human beings have the capacity to observe experience without being caught up in it. This means simply that it is possible to observe ourselves having a craving, or a happy thought, or even a scary emotion, without reacting in the moment in a way that amplifies the feeling or sends the mind spiraling off into thinking about old memories or anticipating events.
paragraphs.cn: 这种练习基于古代佛教文本中首次描述的一种洞见,即人类有能力观察体验而不陷入其中。这简单地意味 着,我们可以观察自己产生渴望、快乐的想法,甚至可怕的情绪,而不在当下以放大这种感受或使思绪陷入对 旧回忆的思考或对未来事件的预期的方式做出反应。

paragraphs.en: This practice of mindfulness can help calm the mind and the body as we learn not to react to experience with likes and dislikes or judgments of good and bad. It does not make us cold or indifferent but more fully present.
paragraphs.cn: 这种正念练习可以帮助平静身心,因为我们学会不以好恶或好坏的判断来回应体验。它不会使我们变得冷漠 或漠不关心,而是让我们更充分地活在当下。

paragraphs.en: One of the challenges of practicing mindfulness in our contemporary world is that there has been a profound transformation in human attention. The artist Jenny Odell argues that in our "attention economy" human attention has been transformed into a commodity that big corporations buy and sell. This economy rests on a technological revolution of mobile phones and social media that makes it possible for corporations to target our attention with their content at every moment.
paragraphs.cn: 在当代世界练习正念的挑战之一是人类注意力发生了深刻的转变。艺术家Jenny Odell认为,在我们的"注意 力经济"中,人类注意力已经转变为大公司买卖的商品。这种经济依赖于移动电话和社交媒体的技术革命,使 公司能够在每时每刻用其内容瞄准我们的注意力。

paragraphs.en: The devices most people use are a perpetual diversion from the present moment. The result is that it can feel as though our ability to focus, and be fully present, has been stolen. But mindfulness can help us resist the attention economy and relish the things that make life special, like being together with those we love.
paragraphs.cn: 大多数人使用的设备是对当下时刻的永久分散。其结果是,我们的专注能力和充分活在当下的能力似乎被偷 走了。但正念可以帮助我们抵制注意力经济,并珍视那些使生活特别的事物,比如与我们所爱的人在一起。

paragraphs.en: Most mindfulness research focuses on the individual benefits of the practice, but some scholars assert that we can not only practice mindfulness for ourselves but also practice it for others. It can help us build stronger, healthier relationships.
paragraphs.cn: 大多数正念研究关注这种练习的个人益处,但一些学者断言,我们不仅可以为自己练习正念,也可以为他人练 习正念。它可以帮助我们建立更牢固、更健康的关系。

paragraphs.en: The sad truth is that living in the attention economy, most of us have become bad listeners. However, just as it is possible to watch ourselves having an experience without reacting, it's possible to watch another person have an experience without getting tied up in reactivity and judgment.
paragraphs.cn: 可悲的事实是,生活在注意力经济中,我们大多数人已经成为糟糕的倾听者。然而,正如我们可以观察自己拥 有一种体验而不做出反应一样,我们也可以观察另一个人拥有一种体验而不陷入反应性和判断之中。

paragraphs.en: The gift of mindfulness is a practice of listening with compassion to others describe their experiences. To give this gift means putting away your phone, turning off social media, and setting aside other common distractions. It means practicing being fully present in another person's presence and listening to them with complete attention without judgment, while resisting the urge to make the interaction about you.
paragraphs.cn: 正念的馈赠是一种带着同情心倾听他人描述其体验的练习。给予这份馈赠意味着收起手机,关闭社交媒体, 并放下其他常见的干扰。它意味着练习在他人面前充分活在当下,并以完全的注意力倾听他们而不加判断, 同时抵制使互动围绕自己的冲动。

paragraphs.en: If we judge the value of gifts based on their price, this gift may seem worthless, but in a distracted world, it is a precious one.
paragraphs.cn: 如果我们根据价格来判断礼物的价值,这份礼物可能看起来毫无价值,但在一个分心的世界里,它是珍贵的。

paragraphs.en: The other day I had to log into a service I hadn't used before. Since I was a new user, the website decided that it needed to check I wasn't a robot and so set me a Captcha test to determine whether the user is a person or a machine.
paragraphs.cn: 前几天我不得不登录一个之前从未使用过的服务。由于我是新用户,该网站决定需要检查我不是机器人,于 是让我完成一项验证码测试来确定用户是人还是机器。

paragraphs.en: I was presented with an image of a roadside scene over which was laid a grid. My "challenge" was to click on each cell in the grid that contained a traffic sign. I did so, a bit irritated. Then I was presented with another image and another grid - also with a request to identify road signs. Like a lamb, I complied, after which the website accepted my input.
paragraphs.cn: 我看到一张路边场景的图片,上面覆盖着一个网格。我的"挑战"是点击网格中包含交通标志的每个单元格。 我有点恼火地照做了。然后我又看到另一张图片和另一个网格——同样要求识别道路标志。我像只羔羊一 样顺从了,之后网站接受了我的输入。

paragraphs.en: And then I realised what I had been doing was adding to a dataset for training the machine-learning software that guides self-driving cars. So, to gain access to an automated service that will benefit financially from my input, I first have to do some unpaid labor to help improve the performance of autonomous vehicles.
paragraphs.cn: 然后我意识到我一直在做的事情是为训练指导自动驾驶汽车的机器学习软件添加数据集。所以,为了获得 一项将从我的输入中获得经济利益的自动化服务,我首先必须做一些无偿劳动来帮助提高自动驾驶车辆的 性能。

paragraphs.en: Neat, eh? But note also the delicious additional irony that the Captcha is described as an "automated Turing test". The Turing test was conceived, you may recall, as a way of enabling humans to determine whether a machine could respond in such a way that one couldn't tell whether it was a human or a robot. So we have wandered into a world in which machines make us do tricks to prove that we are humans!
paragraphs.cn: 巧妙,是吧?但也请注意额外的绝妙讽刺,验证码被描述为"自动化图灵测试"。你可能记得,图灵测试的设想是 一种让人类能够确定机器是否能以一种无法分辨它是人还是机器人的方式做出反应的方法。所以我们已经 步入了一个机器让我们做把戏来证明我们是人类的世界!

paragraphs.en: The strangest aspect of this unparalleled shift is how under-discussed it has been. The metaphor of the boiling frog comes to mind. Have we become so subtly conditioned by digital technology that we don't see what's been happening to us? Have we been conditioned to accept a world governed by "smart" tech, trading convenience to the point where we become a bit like machines ourselves?
paragraphs.cn: 这一史无前例转变最奇怪的方面是它讨论得如此之少。温水煮青蛙的比喻浮现在脑海中。我们是否已经被 数字技术如此微妙地训化,以至于我们看不到发生在我们身上的事情?我们是否已经被训化到接受一个由"智 能"技术统治的世界,为了便利而交易到我们自己都变得有点像机器的地步?

paragraphs.en: In a recent startling and thoughtful book, two scholars - Brett Frischmann, a law professor, and Evan Selinger, a philosopher - argue that the answer to that question is "yes".
paragraphs.cn: 在最近一本令人震惊且发人深省的书中,两位学者——法学教授Brett Frischmann和哲学家Evan Selinger ——认为这个问题的答案是"是的"。

paragraphs.en: And they're right. There's nothing technophobic (技术恐惧的) about that. We shape our tools and then our tools shape us. Technology is supposed to provide tools that serve human ends. But, as the machine-learning Captcha demonstrates, a significant proportion of digital tech now sees (and uses) humans as means to ends that are not ours. In the process, they reduce us to the status of cheery rats running on treadmills (踏车) designed by people who do not have our interests at heart. So back to the frog metaphor. Are we smart enough to jump out before it's too late? You don't even have to Google it to know the answer.
paragraphs.cn: 他们是对的。这并没有任何技术恐惧的成分。我们塑造我们的工具,然后我们的工具塑造我们。技术本应提 供服务于人类目的的工具。但是,正如机器学习验证码所展示的,相当大比例的数字技术现在将人类视为(并 利用为)达成并非我们自己目的的手段。在这个过程中,它们把我们降低到快乐地在由不以我们利益为重的 人设计的踏车上奔跑的老鼠的地位。所以回到青蛙的比喻。我们是否足够聪明在为时已晚之前跳出来?你 甚至不必谷歌搜索就知道答案。

writing.modelEssay:
In an era of rapid social development, it is vitally important to enhance young people's sense of responsibility.
As society changes at an unprecedented pace, young people often face distractions and pressures that weaken
their commitment to family, community, and the future. Without a strong sense of responsibility, they may
become self-centered and short-sighted.
The decline of responsibility among youth is partly caused by the instant gratification culture brought by
technology and social media. Many young people are used to receiving immediate rewards and may avoid
duties that require long-term effort. To address this problem, schools and families should work together to
cultivate accountability through real tasks and role models. For example, involving students in community
service can help them understand the value of contributing to society.
In conclusion, enhancing young people's sense of responsibility is not only a personal virtue but also a social
necessity. Only when the younger generation takes responsibility seriously can society achieve sustainable
development and harmony.
writing.modelCn:
在社会快速发展的时代，提升年轻人的责任感至关重要。随着社会以前所未有的速度变化，年轻人常常面
临分散注意力和压力，这些因素削弱了他们对家庭、社区和未来的承诺。如果没有强烈的责任感，他们可
能会变得以自我为中心、目光短浅。
年轻人责任感的下降，部分是由科技和社交媒体带来的即时满足文化造成的。许多年轻人习惯于获得即时
回报，可能会回避需要长期付出的职责。为解决这一问题，学校和家庭应共同努力，通过真实任务和榜样
示范来培养责任意识。例如，让学生参与社区服务，可以帮助他们理解为社会做贡献的价值。
总之，提升年轻人的责任感不仅是个人美德，也是社会必需。只有当年轻一代认真对待责任时，社会才能
实现可持续发展与和谐。

translation.source: 电子商务的蓬勃发展正在深刻改变中国农村的面貌。随着互联网和物流网络快速向农村延伸，  越来越多的农村居民通过电子商务平台将农产品直接销售给城市消费者。近年来，直播带货  ( live-streaming commerce) 使城市消费者能够与卖家实时互动，已成为促进农村发展的一种新方式。电子商务打破了城乡之间的信息壁垒，拓宽了农产品销售渠道，帮助农村居民增收致富。数字经济与乡村振兴的深度融合，正在为中国农村发展注入前所未有的活力。
translation.reference: The booming development of e-commerce is profoundly changing the face of rural China. As the Internet and logistics networks rapidly extend into rural areas, more and more rural residents are selling their agricultural products directly to urban consumers through e-commerce platforms. In recent years, live-streaming commerce, which enables urban consumers to interact with sellers in real time, has become a new way to promote rural development. E-commerce has broken down the information barriers between urban and rural areas and expanded sales channels for agricultural products, helping rural residents increase their incomes and achieve prosperity. The deep integration of the digital economy with rural revitalization is injecting unprecedented vitality into China's rural development.
