match.title: How do you bring a forest back to life?

A.en: Five hundred years ago, forests covered much of the Iberian peninsula. But that soon changed. Centuries of wars and invasions, agricultural expansion and woodcutting for firewood and shipping wiped out most of the woods and transformed places like Matamorisca, a small village in northern Spain, into degraded landscapes.
A.cn: 五百年前，森林覆盖了伊比利亚半岛的大部分地区。但这种情况很快发生了改变。数百年的战争和入 侵、农业扩张，以及为取暖和造船而砍伐木材，使大部分森林消失，并将西班牙北部的小村庄 Matamorisca等地变成了退化的景观。

B.en: The region's dry climate and depleted soils would be a recipe for disaster in your average program to replant trees, but for the Amsterdam-based Land Life Company it's an ideal place. "We typically operate where nature does not come back by itself," says Jurrian Ruys, its CEO. "We go where there are rougher conditions in terms of weather, with rough or very hot summers." In Matamorisca, they intervened in 17 barren hectares owned by the regional government and peppered them with their signature device: a biodegradable (可生 物 降 解的) cardboard container they call the cocoon which can hold 25 litres of water underground to aid a seedling's first year. Around 16,000 trees, including oaks, ashes, walnuts, rowans, and whitebeams, were planted in May 2018, and the company reports that 96% of them survived that year's burning hot summer without extra irrigation, a critical milestone for a young tree.
B.cn: signature device: a biodegradable( 可⽣物降解的 ) cardboard container they call the cocoon which can 该地区干燥的气候和贫瘠的土壤，对于一般的植树造林计划来说将是灾难的根源，但对于总部位于阿 姆斯特丹的Land Life Company而言，这里却是理想之地。该公司的首席执行官Jurrian Ruys说：“我 们通常在自然无法自行恢复的地方开展工作。我们会前往天气条件更为恶劣、夏季较为艰苦或极其炎 热的地方。”在Matamorisca，他们对地方政府拥有的17公顷贫瘠土地进行了干预，并在其中布置了 他们的标志性设备：一种可生物降解的纸板容器，他们称之为“茧”，可以在地下储存25升水，以帮助 幼苗度过第一年。2018年5月，他们种下了约1.6万棵树，包括橡树、白蜡树、核桃树、花楸树和白檀 树。公司报告称，其中96%的树木在当年酷热的夏季中没有额外灌溉也存活了下来，这对幼树而言是 一个关键的里程碑。

C.en: "Does nature return by itself?" asks Arnout Asjes, Land Life Company's chief technology officer, who oversees a mix of drone (无人机) and satellite imagery, big data analysis, soil enhancement, QR (二维码) tagging and site-specific tree configuration designs. "Probably, but it can take decades or hundreds of years, so we are speeding things up."
C.cn: oversees a mix of drone( ⽆⼈机 ) and satellite imagery, big data analysis, soil enhancement, QR( ⼆维 Land Life Company的首席技术官Arnout Asjes负责统筹无人机和卫星影像、大数据分析、土壤改 良、二维码标记以及因地制宜的树木配置设计。他问道：“自然会自行恢复吗？或许会，但可能需要几 十年甚至几百年，所以我们正在加快这一进程。”

D.en: His company belongs to a global movement of organisations trying to save degraded or deforested areas, ranging from fertile tropical lowlands to dry hills in temperate (温带的) regions. Spurred by global biodiversity loss and climate change, these groups are pushing the boundary of how to revive forest cover. "It's not a theoretical proposition," says Walter Vergara, a forest and climate specialist at the World Resources Institute (WRI). "It requires the right incentives, the right stakeholders, the right analysis and sufficient capital, but it can happen."
D.cn: areas, ranging from fertile tropical lowlands to dry hills in temperate( 温带的 ) regions. Spurred by 他的公司属于一个全球性运动，该运动由一系列试图拯救退化或遭到砍伐的地区的组织组成，这些地 区从肥沃的热带低地到温带地区的干燥丘陵不等。在全球生物多样性丧失和气候变化的推动下，这些 组织正在拓展恢复森林覆盖的可能性。世界资源研究所（WRI）的森林与气候专家Walter Vergara 说：“这不是一个理论上的设想。它需要正确的激励机制、正确的利益相关者、正确的分析和充足的资 金，但这是可以实现的。”

E.en: How these factors come together for a particular project - and whether saving destroyed woods is even possible - depends on what kind of ecosystem you have in mind. Secondary forests in the Amazon are different from Texas pines recovering after wildfires or the Arctic timber woods that cover much of Sweden. Each provides different reasons for reforestation programs and each has particular needs. In the dry conditions around Matamorisca and similar areas in Spain, Land Life Company worries about rapid desertification (沙漠化). As its focus is on restoring an ecosystem, it works with organisations that don't expect their money back.
E.cn: Company worries about rapid desertification( 沙漠化 ). As its focus is on restoring an ecosystem, it 这些因素如何结合到某个具体项目中，以及拯救遭到破坏的森林是否真的可行，取决于你设想的生态 系统类型。亚马孙地区的次生林，与野火后正在恢复的得克萨斯州松林，或覆盖瑞典大部分地区的北 极森林，都各不相同。每种生态系统都有不同的理由促使人们实施重新造林计划，也各自有特别的需 求。在Matamorisca周边及西班牙类似地区的干燥环境中，Land Life Company担心的是迅速发生的 沙漠化。由于该公司的重点是恢复生态系统，因此它与那些不指望收回资金的组织合作。

F.en: With around 600 hectares replanted around the world since 2015 and another 1,100 planned for this year, the company's drive fits into the Bonn Challenge, a global effort to restore 150 million hectares of the world's deforested and degraded land by 2020. That's an area roughly the size of Iran or Mongolia. By 2030, the goal is to reach 350 million hectares - 20% more land than India. These targets include both the rehabilitation of forested areas that have lost density or look a bit weak (a process known as "restoration" in forestry jargon) and the recovery of forest cover in areas where it was completely cleared (what's known as "reforestation").
F.cn: 自2015年以来，该公司已在世界各地重新种植了约600公顷土地，今年还计划再种植1100公顷，这项 事业与“波恩挑战”相契合。“波恩挑战”是一项全球性行动，旨在到2020年恢复世界上1.5亿公顷被砍伐 和退化的土地。这一面积大致相当于伊朗或蒙古的国土面积。到2030年，目标是达到3.5亿公顷，比印 度的国土面积多20%。这些目标既包括对森林密度下降或状况有所衰退的林区进行修复（林业术语称 为“恢复”），也包括在森林覆盖曾被完全清除的地区恢复森林覆盖（即所谓的“重新造林”）。

G.en: That global target is broken into smaller pieces and takes shape in Latin America as the 20x20 Initiative, an effort to contribute 20 million hectares to the overall goal by initiating small to medium projects with the political backing of governments. Unlike Land Life Company, this region-wide project makes the economic and business case for reforestation, even though they are after biodiversity conservation. "You need to bring in private sector money," says WRI's Vergara, who leads the initiative, "and that capital needs to see a return on their investment." A study he led predicts Latin America would see an estimated net present value of about $23 bn over a 50-year period if it reaches its goal.
G.cn: 这一全球目标被分解成更小的部分，在拉丁美洲则以“20x20倡议”的形式展开。这项倡议在各国政府的 政治支持下，通过启动中小型项目，为总体目标贡献2000万公顷土地。与Land Life Company不同， 这一覆盖整个地区的项目着眼于重新造林的经济和商业价值，尽管其目的在于保护生物多样性。负责 领导该倡议的世界资源研究所Vergara说：“你需要引入私营部门的资金，而这些资金需要看到投资回 报。”他领导的一项研究预测，如果拉丁美洲实现这一目标，那么在50年间预计可获得约230亿美元的 净现值。

H.en: Money can come from timber sales in sustainably managed forests or from harvesting "non-wood products" like nuts, oils and fruits from the trees. You can take note of how much carbon dioxide your forest is capturing and sell carbon credits to companies keen to offset their emissions. Or you can even grow the forest hoping that biodiversity will attract ecotourists who'd pay for lodging, birdwatching tours and meals.
H.cn: 资金可以来自可持续经营森林的木材销售，也可以来自采集树上的坚果、油料和水果等“非木材产 品”。你可以记录森林吸收了多少二氧化碳，并向那些急于抵消自身排放的公司出售碳信用额度。或 者，你甚至可以培育森林，希望生物多样性能够吸引生态旅游者，让他们为住宿、观鸟之旅和餐饮 付费。

I.en: Still, these backers are not your high-street bank. Money for the 20x20 Initiative comes mostly from financial organisations with triple goals - a modest return on their investment, environmental benefits and social gains - known as impact investors. Take the German fund 12Tree for instance, one of the 20x20 partners. It put $9.5 million into Cuango, a 1,455-hectare property on the Caribbean coast of Panama that combines a commercial cocoa tree plantation with timber extraction from a sustainably managed secondary forest. With their money, they reforested a former cattle ranch, provided high-quality jobs for the surrounding communities and made a return on their investment.
I.cn: 不过，这些支持者并不是普通的商业银行。“20x20倡议”的资金主要来自具有三重目标的金融机构：获 得适度的投资回报、取得环境效益以及实现社会收益，这些机构被称为影响力投资者。以德国基金 12Tree为例，它是“20x20倡议”的合作伙伴之一。该基金向Cuango投入了950万美元。Cuango位于巴 拿马加勒比海沿岸，占地1455公顷，将商业可可种植园与从可持续经营的次生林中采伐木材结合起 来。借助这笔资金，他们在一处曾经的牧牛场上重新造林，为周边社区提供了高质量的就业机会，并获 得了投资回报。

J.en: Even on land cleared decades ago and currently used by farmers, some crops can coexist with the forest, if you find the right balance. Although not technically reforestation, agroforestry (a system of land use in which harvestable trees or shrubs are grown among or around crops or on pasture land, as a means of preserving or enhancing the productivity of the land) provides an opportunity for small-holder farmers to sustain their livelihoods while adding some forest cover to their farms.
J.cn: 即使是在数十年前被清理、目前由农民使用的土地上，只要找到适当的平衡，一些农作物也可以与森 林共存。农林业虽然在技术上不属于重新造林，但它是一种土地利用系统，即在农作物之间或周围、 或者牧场上种植可采收的树木或灌木，以保持或提高土地的生产力。它为小农户维持生计提供了机 会，同时也能在农场中增加一定的森林覆盖。

K.en: A global project called Breedcafs is studying how trees behave in coffee farms, hoping to find crop varieties that manage to grow under the shade of trees. Coffee grows naturally in such forests, so copying that in farms is taking the crop back to its roots. "By reintroducing trees in the landscape, we impact positively humidity, rain capture, soil conservation and biodiversity preservation," says coffee expert Benoît Bertrand, who leads the project from the French Agricultural Research Centre for International Development. Bertrand is analysing which of dozens of coffee varieties fits better for this system. A similar approach can be applied to land with cocoa, vanilla and fruit trees.
K.cn: 一项名为Breedcafs的全球性项目正在研究树木在咖啡农场中的生长状况，希望找到能够在树荫下生 长的作物品种。咖啡在这类森林中自然生长，因此在农场中复制这种环境，就是让这种作物回归其根 源。该项目由法国国际发展农业研究中心的咖啡专家Benoit Bertrand负责。他说：“通过在景观中重 新引入树木，我们能够积极改善湿度、雨水截留、土壤保护和生物多样性保护。”Bertrand正在分析 数十种咖啡品种，以确定哪一种更适合这一系统。类似的方法也可以应用于种植可可、香草和果树的 土地。

L.en: Not every piece of land is fit for reforestation. Vergara's partners look for safe investments, and even Land Life Company only runs major projects in what they consider "low-risk" countries. "We tend to avoid large-scale operations in countries in some parts of the Middle East or Africa where the permanence is not secured," says Ruys.
L.cn: 并非每一块土地都适合重新造林。Vergara的合作伙伴寻找的是安全的投资，甚至Land Life Company也只在他们认为“低风险”的国家开展大型项目。Ruys说：“在中东或非洲的一些国家，由于 无法确保森林的长期存续，我们往往会避免在那里开展大规模项目。”

M.en: But in the right location, perhaps all you need is time. In the Central Pacific of Costa Rica, the 330-hectare National Wildlife Refuge Barú looks nothing like the cattle ranch it was before 1987, when Jack Ewing decided to turn this large estate into an ecotourism destination. Instead of intervening, a friend told him to let nature have its way. Barú's former grazing lands are now thriving woods and the property boasts over 150 hectares of secondary forests with no intervention from humans. In the past 10 years, animals such as howling monkeys, scarlet macaws and even migratory cougars have returned to the refuge's land, boosting tourism and revitalising the ecosystem. Ewing, now 75, explains this success using the words his friend chose three decades ago: "In Costa Rica, when you stop managing the shrubs, the jungle comes back for its revenge."

statements.locateCn: 的合作伙伴寻找安全投资，就连 Land Life Company 也只在他们认为「低风险」 的国家开展重大项目。「我们倾向于避免在中东或非洲部分国家开展大规模行动，因为那里 的持久性无法得到保障，」Ruys 说。

statements.text: Left alone, nature may take scores of years or even centuries to repair itself.
statements.locateEn: "Does nature return by itself?" asks Arnout Asjes, Land Life Company's chief technology officer, who oversees a mix of drone and satellite imagery, big data analysis, soil enhancement, QR tagging and site-specific tree configuration designs. "Probably, but it can take decades or hundreds of years, so we are speeding things up."
statements.locateCn: 自然能自行恢复吗？Land Life Company 的首席技术官 Arnout Asjes 问道，他负责监 管无人机与卫星图像、大数据分析、土壤改良、二维码标签和因地制宜的树木配置设计。 可能可以，但这需要数十年或数百年，所以我们正在加速这一过程。

statements.text: Economic returns can be derived from selling timber and non-wood products as well as carbon
statements.locateEn: Money can come from timber sales in sustainably managed forests or from harvesting 'non- wood products' like nuts, oils and fruits from the trees. You can take note of how much carbon dioxide your forest is capturing and sell carbon credits to companies keen to offset their emissions. Or you can even grow the forest hoping that biodiversity will attract ecotourists who'd pay for lodging, birdwatching tours and meals.
statements.locateCn: 资金可以来自可持续管理森林中的木材销售，或从树上收获「非木材产品」如坚果、油和水 果。你可以记录森林吸收了多少二氧化碳，然后把碳信用卖给希望抵消排放的公司。或者你 甚至可以培育森林，寄望生物多样性会吸引愿意支付住宿、观鸟旅行和餐饮费用的生态旅 游者。

statements.text: A study is under way across the world to look for crops that can grow among trees.
statements.locateEn: A global project called Breedcafs is studying how trees behave in coffee farms, hoping to find crop varieties that manage to grow under the shade of trees. Coffee grows naturally in such forests, so copying that in farms is taking the crop back to its roots. 'By reintroducing trees in the landscape, we impact positively humidity, rain capture, soil conservation and biodiversity preservation,' says coffee expert Benoit Bertrand, who leads the project from the French Agricultural Research Centre for International Development. Bertrand is analysing which of dozens of coffee varieties fits better for this system.
statements.locateCn: 一个名为 Breedcafs 的全球项目正在研究咖啡农场中树木的生长情况，希望找到能在树荫下 生长的作物品种。咖啡天然生长于这样的森林中，因此在农场中模仿这种做法等于让作物回 归本源。「通过在景观中重新引入树木，我们积极影响湿度、雨水截留、土壤保护和生物多 样性保护，」在法国农业国际合作研究中心领导该项目的咖啡专家 Benoit Bertrand 说。 Bertrand 正在分析数十种咖啡品种中哪一种更适合这一系统。

statements.text: Land Life Company's operations are usually located where reforestation is impossible without human
statements.locateEn: The region's dry climate and depleted soils would be a recipe for disaster in your average program to replant trees, but for the Amsterdam-based Land Life Company it's an ideal place. 'We typically operate where nature does not come back by itself,' says Jurrian Ruys, its CEO. 'We go where there are rougher conditions in terms of weather, with rough or very hot summers.'
statements.locateCn: 该地区干燥的气候和贫瘠的土壤对普通的植树项目来说会是灾难配方，但对总部位于阿姆斯 特丹的 Land Life Company 而言却是理想之地。「我们通常在大自然无法自行恢复的地方 作业，」其首席执行官 Jurrian Ruys 说，「我们去气候条件更恶劣的地方，那里夏季炎热 或酷暑。」 45.Land Life Company's operations are usually located where reforestation is impossible without human intervention.

paragraphs.en: What does self-discipline look like at work? Sometimes, it's the ability to resist temptation, such as distractions to avoid a particular task. Other times it's the ability to persist with a task when your energy and motivation seem low.
paragraphs.cn: 在工作中，自律是什么样的表现？有时，它是抵制诱惑的能力，比如抵制那些让你逃避某项特定任务的干 扰。还有些时候，它是在精力和动力似乎都很低的时候，仍然坚持完成一项任务的能力。

paragraphs.en: What do you believe about the nature of your own self-discipline? Is it something that runs on internal energy that is spent with use? Or is it something that is bolstered as you apply it and persist?
paragraphs.cn: 你如何看待自身自律的本质？它是否依靠一种会随着使用而消耗的内在能量运行？还是说，它会在你运用 自律并坚持下去的过程中得到增强？

paragraphs.en: Your answer matters, as it determines how much self-discipline you experience. For years, research in psychology pointed to self-control as a resource that is depleted with use and needs to be restored through breaks, rest, or sleep. More recently, however, research points to the importance of mindset. If you view self-discipline as an expendable resource, your willpower tends to fade with use. If you believe that exercising your self-control strengthens and fuels it, that is more likely to be your experience as you resist temptation or push yourself to get something done that is not appealing.
paragraphs.cn: 你的答案很重要，因为它决定了你能体验到多少自律。多年来，心理学研究认为，自我控制是一种会因使 用而消耗、需要通过休息、放松或睡眠来恢复的资源。然而，近来的研究更加重视思维方式的重要性。如 果你把自律看作一种会耗尽的资源，你的意志力往往会随着使用而减弱。如果你相信运用自我控制能够 增强并补充它，那么当你抵制诱惑，或迫使自己完成一件并不吸引人的事情时，你更有可能获得这样的 体验。

paragraphs.en: If you don't already view self-discipline as a force that feeds itself, what might you do? Reflect on times that you had initial difficulty resisting temptation, getting started on something, or sticking with it, but pushed ahead and accomplished the task or met the goal. That's the kind of experience we're talking about with this particular belief about self-discipline, and you've already had such an experience, so you've shown that it's possible. When you feel your willpower and motivation fading, remind yourself of those previous experiences and imagine the same happening now.
paragraphs.cn: 如果你还没有把自律看作一种能够自我补充的力量，可以做些什么呢？回想一下这样的时刻：起初你很难 抵制诱惑、开始做某件事，或者坚持做下去，但后来你还是继续努力，完成了任务或实现了目标。这正是 我们所说的关于自律的这种特定信念所对应的经历，而你已经有过这样的经历，所以你已经证明了这是可 能的。当你感到意志力和动力逐渐消退时，提醒自己想起以往的这些经历，并想象现在也会发生同样的 情况。

paragraphs.en: What if your experiences have always seemed to indicate that your self-control diminishes with use, and you need breaks to recharge? There's nothing wrong with that as long as you can afford to take those breaks. If not, remind yourself that not everyone experiences self-discipline as a depletable resource and that your experience might be different if you focus on gathering more energy at this point rather than focusing on how difficult it is to continue or the need for a break.
paragraphs.cn: 如果你的经历一直表明，你的自我控制会随着使用而减弱，需要通过休息来充电，那该怎么办？只要你有 条件休息，这本身没有什么问题。如果没有条件，那么就提醒自己，并非每个人都会把自律体验为一种会 耗尽的资源；如果此时你把注意力放在积蓄更多能量上，而不是关注继续下去有多么困难或认为自己需要 休息，你的体验可能会有所不同。

paragraphs.en: Also, if you know someone who is a role model of self-discipline, picture that person in your situation, persisting in the task. Regardless of how you do it, as you push forward to continue to accomplish progress, be sure to mentally reinforce yourself by taking pride in your ability to exert more willpower as you persist.
paragraphs.cn: 此外，如果你认识一位自律方面的榜样，可以想象那个人处在你的情境中，坚持完成这项任务。无论你采 用什么方式，当你继续向前、不断取得进展时，一定要通过为自己能够在坚持过程中发挥出更强的意志力 而感到自豪，在心理上不断强化自己。

paragraphs.en: The benefits of exerting willpower are cumulative. Your self-discipline is akin to a muscle, and each time you resist temptation or persist in a task despite a lack of motivation, you strengthen that muscle, leading to less effort and resistance in similar instances in the future.
paragraphs.cn: 发挥意志力所带来的益处会不断累积。你的自律就像一块肌肉，每当你抵制诱惑，或在缺乏动力的情况下 仍坚持完成一项任务时，你都会锻炼并强化这块肌肉，从而使自己在今后遇到类似情况时付出更少的努 力，也能减少阻力。

paragraphs.en: Smartphones have always posed challenges for parents of teens. From social media apps to excessive screen time, the digital world is as threatening as the physical.
paragraphs.cn: 智能手机一直给青少年父母带来挑战。从社交媒体应用到过度使用屏幕，数字世界和现实世界一样具有威 胁性。

paragraphs.en: A new study shows that about half of parents of teens are worried about their teens being exposed to explicit content online. This is a valid concern, of course. But there are ways to alleviate the spread of explicit content, from changing the settings in their kids' phone to monitoring such content with apps like Bark.
paragraphs.cn: 一项新的研究显示，大约一半的青少年父母担心自己的孩子会在网上接触到露骨内容。当然，这种担忧是 合理的。但是，有一些方法可以减缓露骨内容的传播，比如更改孩子手机中的设置，或使用 Bark 等应用 监控这类内容。

paragraphs.en: Just as alarming, if not more so, is that the amount of time teens spend on social media can lead to anxiety and depression.
paragraphs.cn: 同样令人担忧，甚至更加令人担忧的是，青少年花在社交媒体上的时间可能会导致焦虑和抑郁。

paragraphs.en: Excessive screen time has detrimental effects, for a lot of obvious reasons. Constant media consumption inhibits healthy activities associated with childhood, like spending time outside, exercising, talking to friends and family. If it interferes with sleep, that's even worse.
paragraphs.cn: 过度使用屏幕会产生不利影响，原因有很多，而且显而易见。持续接触媒体会妨碍童年时期与健康相关的 活动，例如待在户外、锻炼以及与朋友和家人交谈。如果它还干扰睡眠，那就更糟糕了。

paragraphs.en: Ample research shows too much smartphone use produces significant anxiety, depression, and feelings of isolation in teens. Teens log on to social media or spend time online trying to make connections, but end up feeling more alone and sadder than ever. Faceless communication not only produces feelings of isolation and loneliness but increases instances of online bullying and susceptibility to criminal conducts.
paragraphs.cn: 大量研究表明，过度使用智能手机会使青少年产生严重的焦虑、抑郁和孤立感。青少年登录社交媒体或上 网，试图建立联系，但最终却比以往任何时候都感到更加孤独和悲伤。无面对面的交流不仅会产生孤立感 和孤独感，还会增加网络欺凌事件以及受犯罪行为影响的可能性。

paragraphs.en: Though I've banned most social media, I've still battled smartphone time with my own kids. A lot of the time I wish I could throw my kids' smartphones into the nearest lake. The convenience of communication - when they need a ride home from school after practice, for instance - often feels like it isn't worth the battle to keep their screen time low and productive, and continue to encourage "real-life" activities outside and with friends and family. I understand the addiction and often tell them I'm not sure how I would have handled having a smartphone as a teen. As an adult, I too, struggle with overuse.
paragraphs.cn: 虽然我已经禁止使用大多数社交媒体，但我仍然一直在和自己的孩子争论使用智能手机的时间。很多时 候，我真希望能把孩子们的智能手机扔进最近的湖里。通信的便利性——比如他们课外活动结束后需要搭 车回家时——常常让人觉得，为了控制他们的屏幕使用时间，使其保持较低水平并发挥积极作用，同时继 续鼓励他们在户外以及与朋友和家人进行“现实生活”活动，并不值得这样争斗。我理解这种成瘾，而且常 常告诉他们，我不知道自己在青少年时期拥有一部智能手机会如何应对。作为一个成年人，我也在努力应 对过度使用的问题。

paragraphs.en: In a recent TV interview to promote a new film about a mother and daughter navigating social media use, actress Kate Winslet expressed her view on teens and social media - and her concern mirrors the trends. "I do definitely feel that the world of social media is frightening to parents because we don't really know what's there," she said. "We don't know how our children are using it. We don't know the effects that it's really having on them."
paragraphs.cn: 在最近一次为宣传一部讲述母女共同应对社交媒体使用问题的新电影而进行的电视采访中，女演员凯特·温 斯莱特表达了她对青少年和社交媒体的看法，而她的担忧与相关趋势相一致。她说：“我确实觉得，社交 媒体的世界令父母感到害怕，因为我们并不真正知道那里有什么。我们不知道自己的孩子是如何使用它 的。我们不知道它究竟会对他们产生什么影响。”

paragraphs.en: I don't think the US government should regulate social media and teen smartphone use, but it is a vital topic for parents to understand and take seriously. Unfortunately, now, parents don't just have to worry about real-world dangers, but all the ones sneaking online and the effects they have on teenagers and their mental health.
paragraphs.cn: 我认为美国政府不应监管社交媒体和青少年使用智能手机的问题，但这是一个父母必须了解并认真对待的 重要话题。遗憾的是，如今父母不仅要担心现实世界中的危险，还要担心所有悄悄潜入网络的危险，以及 这些危险对青少年及其心理健康造成的影响。

segments.en: Hi, Frank, are you working through your lunch hour again?

segments.speaker: M
segments.en: No, not at all. It's my 10th wedding anniversary next week, and I promised Jane that I would book a city break for us, as I have annual leave to take, and it would be nice to celebrate somewhere warm. So, I'm trying to book something in Barcelona.
segments.cn: 不，完全不是。我和简下周要过结婚十周年纪念日了，我答应过她要为我们预订一次城市短途旅行， 因为我还有年假要休，而且能找个温暖的地方庆祝一下也不错。所以，我正在设法预订去巴塞罗那的 行程。

segments.speaker: W
segments.en: That sounds so romantic. I adore Barcelona. It's such a fabulous cosmopolitan city. There's so much to do there, excellent food, and that cathedral that they are still building after about 150 years. Very cool.
segments.cn: 听起来真浪漫。我非常喜欢巴塞罗那。那是一座非常棒的国际化城市。那里有很多事情可做，美食也 很棒，还有那座已经修建了大约150年、至今仍在建造的教堂。太酷了。

segments.speaker: M
segments.en: I know. But the anniversary is looming, and I'm still scrambling to find accommodation. Everything is either wildly expensive or already fully booked. I'm starting to feel a bit frantic.
segments.cn: 我知道。但纪念日就要到了，我还在手忙脚乱地找住宿。要么贵得离谱，要么已经全部订满。我开始 有点慌了。

segments.speaker: W
segments.en: Well, if you are going for a whole week, why don't you do a couple of nights in somewhere really glamorous, and then do the rest of the week a bit further up the coast, where the accommodation is cheaper, and that will offset the cost of the expensive place?
segments.cn: 这样吧，如果你们要去整整一周，为什么不先在一个非常豪华的地方住几个晚上，然后把剩下的时间 安排在海岸线再往北一点的地方，那里住宿更便宜，这样就能抵消住昂贵地方的费用了？

segments.speaker: M
segments.en: That might be a good plan. It's not too expensive to rent a car, so we could still drive into the city. Yes, there are lots of places outside the city that have pools and are all inclusive, so we wouldn't even need to pay for food or drinks. I'll send a query now about the dates we're interested in.
segments.cn: 这或许是个不错的计划。租车也不算太贵，所以我们还是可以开车进城。对了，城外有很多地方带游 泳池，而且提供全包服务，这样我们连吃饭和饮料的钱都不用另外付了。我现在就发个咨询，问问我们感 兴趣的日期是否有空。

segments.speaker: W
segments.en: That sounds perfect. I'm sure that Jane will be absolutely thrilled to bits. I really do recommend visiting that cathedral. You can go all the way up to the top of it, but you need to go up a really steep spiral staircase to get there.
segments.cn: 听起来太完美了。我相信简一定会高兴坏的。我真的很推荐去参观那座教堂。你们可以一直登到顶 部，但要到那里必须爬一段非常陡的螺旋楼梯。

segments.speaker: M
segments.en: Considering Jane is terrified of heights, I think if I tried to make her do that, I would come back divorced. Thanks for the help though; it was turning into a logistical nightmare.

segments.en: In America, at least, passion is a word that often comes up on job descriptions and in interviews. On the whole, passionate people are thought of in a positive light and considered likely to achieve their goals. But when it comes to predicting achievement, has the importance of passion been overstated?
segments.cn: 至少在美国，求职描述和面试中经常会提到“热情”一词。总的来说，人们对有热情的人持正面看法，认为 他们很可能实现自己的目标。但说到预测成就时，热情的重要性是否被夸大了？

segments.en: According to a new study from Stanford University, passion may be less important in certain cultures, and the fact that passion is often seen as a key to achievement may reflect a distinctly Western model of motivation. The chief factor explored in the study was how individualistic a society was. In individualistic cultures, the researchers assert, people are more motivated by pursuing paths related to their passions, but those in collectivistic cultures are more likely to see themselves as part of a network. They often place fulfilling obligations to others above focusing on their own interests.
segments.cn: 根据斯坦福大学的一项新研究，热情在某些文化中的重要性可能较低，而热情常被视为成就关键这一事 实，或许反映了一种明显具有西方特色的动机模式。研究考察的主要因素是一个社会的个人主义程度。研 究人员断言，在个人主义文化中，人们更容易受到追求与自身热情相关道路的激励；而集体主义文化中的 人则更可能将自己视为某个社会网络的一部分。他们往往更重视履行对他人的义务，而不是专注于自身的 兴趣。

segments.en: The researchers looked at data from nearly 60 countries. They found that in science subjects, passion was positively correlated with academic achievements. Higher levels of enjoyment and interest also bolstered test scores.
segments.cn: 研究人员考察了来自近60个国家的数据。他们发现，在科学类学科中，热情与学业成就呈正相关。更高程 度的愉悦感和兴趣也会提高测试成绩。

segments.en: But the strength of this correlation wasn't the same across cultures. Those in individualistic societies such as the U.S., Australia, and the UK showed a stronger link between passion and achievement. The effect of passion on performance was more subtle for those in more collectivistic societies such as Colombia or Thailand.
segments.cn: 但这种相关性的强度在不同文化之间并不相同。在美国、澳大利亚和英国等个人主义社会中，热情与成 就之间的联系更为紧密。而对于哥伦比亚或泰国等更加集体主义的社会而言，热情对表现的影响则更为 微妙。

segments.en: These findings were mirrored in achievement in both mathematics and reading. It's clear from the findings that passion isn't the only thing that motivates people to achieve their goals.
segments.cn: 数学和阅读方面的成就也呈现出同样的情况。从这些研究结果可以清楚看出，热情并不是激励人们实现目 标的唯一因素。

segments.en: Why does nature create patterns? The reason patterns often appear in nature is simple: the same basic physical or chemical processes occur in many pattern substances and organisms as they form. Whether in plants and animals or rocks, foams and ice crystals, the intricate patterns that happen in nature come down to what's happening at the level of atoms and molecules.
segments.cn: 为什么自然界会形成各种图案？图案之所以经常出现在自然界中，原因很简单：在许多形成图案的物质和 生物中，相同的基本物理或化学过程会反复发生。无论是在植物和动物中，还是在岩石、泡沫和冰晶中， 自然界中出现的复杂图案，归根结底都与原子和分子层面发生的事情有关。

segments.en: A pattern in nature is any regularly repeated arrangement of shapes or colors. Some of the most striking examples include the six-sided arrays of rocks at Giant's Causeway in the United Kingdom, and the colorful stripes and spots on tropical fish. Patterns like these begin to form at a small scale when materials undergo processes like drying, freezing, wrinkling, diffusing and reacting. Those changes then give rise to complex patterns at a larger scale that people can see.
segments.cn: 自然界中的图案，是指形状或颜色有规律地重复排列的任何形式。其中一些最引人注目的例子包括英国巨 人之路上六边形的岩石阵列，以及热带鱼身上色彩斑斓的条纹和斑点。这类图案在材料经历干燥、冻结、 起皱、扩散和反应等过程时，会先在微小尺度上开始形成。随后，这些变化会在更大尺度上产生人们能够 看见的复杂图案。

segments.en: Imagine delicate frozen crystals on a window during winter. What creates that pattern? When water freezes, its molecules begin clustering together. Water molecules have a particular bent shape that causes them to stack into clusters as they freeze. As the cluster grows, many outside factors, including humidity and temperature, begin to affect its overall shape. If the water is freezing on a window, for example, random imperfections on the glass surface affect the stacking and create the larger pattern.
segments.cn: 想象一下冬天窗户上精致的冰晶。是什么形成了这种图案？水结冰时，其中的分子开始聚集在一起。水分 子具有特殊的弯曲形状，这使它们在冻结时会堆叠成团。随着团簇不断增大，包括湿度和温度在内的许多 外部因素开始影响它的整体形状。例如，如果水是在窗户上结冰，玻璃表面的随机瑕疵就会影响分子的堆 叠，并形成更大的图案。

segments.en: But scientists do not always know the purpose of a pattern, or even if there is one. The molecular processes involved are simple enough that they might generate a pattern by coincidence.
segments.cn: 但科学家并不总是知道某种图案的作用，甚至不知道它是否具有作用。相关的分子过程足够简单，因此它 们可能只是偶然形成了某种图案。

segments.en: Many people, myself included, have multiple areas of life they would like to improve. For example, I would like to reach more people with my writing, to lift heavier weights at the gym, and to start practising mindfulness more consistently. Those are just a few of the goals I find desirable, and you probably have a long list yourself. The problem is, even if we are committed to working hard on our goals, our natural tendency is to return to our old habits at some point. Making a permanent lifestyle change is really difficult.
segments.cn: 包括我在内，许多人都希望改善生活中的多个方面。例如，我希望通过写作让更多人读到我的作品，希望 在健身房举起更重的重量，也希望开始更加持续地练习正念。这些只是我认为值得追求的几个目标，而你 自己可能也列有一长串目标。问题在于，即使我们决心为目标努力奋斗，我们的自然倾向仍然是在某个时 候回到旧有习惯。要永久改变生活方式确实非常困难。

segments.en: Recently I've come across a few studies that will make these difficult lifestyle changes a bit easier. As you'll see, however, the approach to mastering many areas of life is somewhat counterintuitive. Research has shown that you are two to three times more likely to stick with your habits if you make a specific plan for when, where, and how you will perform the behavior. For example, in one study, scientists asked people to fill out a sentence to specify during the next week they would do at least 20 minutes of vigorous exercise on which day, at what time of day, and at or in what place. Researchers found that people who filled out this sentence were two to three times more likely to actually exercise compared to a control group who did not make plans for their future behavior. Psychologists call these specific plans implementation intentions because they state when, where, and how you intend to implement a particular behavior.
segments.cn: 最近，我接触到了一些研究，这些研究将使这些艰难的生活方式改变变得稍微容易一些。不过，正如你将 看到的，掌握生活中许多方面的方法有些违背直觉。研究表明，如果你针对自己将在何时、何地以及如何 实施某种行为制订具体计划，那么坚持这些习惯的可能性会提高到原来的两到三倍。例如，在一项研究 中，科学家要求人们填写一个句子，具体说明自己将在下一周的哪一天、一天中的什么时间，以及在什么 地点进行至少20分钟的剧烈运动。研究人员发现，与没有为未来行为制订计划的对照组相比，填写了这个 句子的人实际进行锻炼的可能性高出两到三倍。心理学家将这些具体计划称为“执行意图”，因为它们说明 了你打算在何时、何地以及如何实施某种特定行为。

segments.en: However, follow-up research has discovered implementation intentions only work when you focus on one thing at a time. In fact, researchers found that people who tried to accomplish multiple goals were less committed and less likely to succeed than those who focused on a single goal.
segments.cn: 然而，后续研究发现，执行意图只有在你一次专注于一件事时才会奏效。事实上，研究人员发现，试图实 现多个目标的人，比专注于单一目标的人投入程度更低，成功的可能性也更小。

segments.en: Another science-based reason to focus on one thing at a time is that when you begin practising a new habit, it requires a lot of conscious effort to remember to do it. After a while, however, the pattern of behavior becomes easier. Eventually, your new habit becomes a normal routine, and the process is more or less mindless and automatic. The most important thing to note is that there is some tipping point at which new habits become more or less automatic. The time it takes to build a habit depends on many factors, including how difficult the habit is, your genetics, and more.
segments.cn: 一次专注于一件事还有一个基于科学的理由，那就是当你开始练习一种新习惯时，记得去做这件事需要付 出大量有意识的努力。然而，过一段时间之后，这种行为模式会变得更加容易。最终，你的新习惯会成为 一种日常惯例，而这一过程或多或少会变得无需意识参与，并且自动进行。需要注意的最重要一点是，存 在这样一个临界点：在此之后，新习惯会或多或少地变得自动化。养成一个习惯所需的时间取决于许多因 素，包括习惯的难度、你的遗传因素，以及其他因素。

segments.en: It was a lazy, hazy, crazy day on the dwarf planet Pluto when New Horizons, a spacecraft from Earth, flew by at a speed of 31,000 mph (miles per hour) two years ago. The spacecraft took a bunch of photos, made some quick measurements of Pluto's atmosphere, and sent them all back here, giving planetary scientists their first up-close look of the distant dwarf planet.
segments.cn: 两年前，在新视野号这艘来自地球的航天器以每小时31,000英里（英里/小时）的速度飞掠而过时，矮行 星冥王星度过了慵懒、朦胧而疯狂的一天。这艘航天器拍摄了大量照片，对冥王星的大气层进行了一些快 速测量，并将这些数据全部传回地球，使行星科学家们首次近距离观察到这颗遥远的矮行星。

segments.en: One of the more bizarre things they found was that the haze in Pluto's atmosphere was much thicker than previously thought. The planet also had an atmosphere much cooler than earlier estimates, topping out at −333.4°F.
segments.cn: 他们发现的较为奇异的现象之一，是冥王星大气层中的霾比先前认为的厚得多。这颗行星的大气层也比早 先估计的冷得多，最高温度仅为−333.4°F。

segments.en: Now, a study published in Nature links those two atmospheric observations. A computer model developed by planetary scientist Xi Zhang and colleagues shows the haze of tiny droplets in the upper atmosphere is likely scattering light from the Sun, preventing heat from reaching the planet below. We see hazy skies on Earth too, from time to time, whenever solid particles get suspended in the air—from water-based fogs, to ash from fires, to the toxic droplets that make up a thick smog. But on Earth, the overall temperature of the planet is dominated by the distribution of gases in our atmosphere.
segments.cn: 如今，《自然》杂志发表的一项研究将这两项大气观测结果联系了起来。行星科学家张希及其同事开发的 一种计算机模型显示，高层大气中由微小液滴形成的霾很可能会散射来自太阳的光，阻止热量抵达下方的 行星。地球上也会不时出现雾霾天气，每当固体颗粒悬浮在空气中时，就可能形成这种现象，从含水雾气 到火灾产生的灰烬，再到构成浓重烟雾的有毒液滴，都是如此。但在地球上，行星的整体温度主要由大气 层中气体的分布决定。

segments.en: On Pluto, the authors suggest, haze might be more influential. Particles can reflect light from the Sun here on Earth: It happens after volcanoes erupt, emitting clouds of particles that reflect the Sun's rays into the atmosphere. Some people even propose imitating this phenomenon to alleviate the effects of climate change. But our planet isn't dominated by that process, or at least it hasn't been for a few billion years.
segments.cn: 作者认为，在冥王星上，霾的影响可能更大。在地球上，颗粒物能够反射来自太阳的光：火山喷发后会释 放出由颗粒物组成的云团，将太阳光线反射回大气层。有些人甚至提出模仿这一现象，以减轻气候变化的 影响。但我们的行星并不是由这一过程主导的，至少在过去几十亿年里不是如此。

segments.en: If Pluto's atmosphere is very different from ours and from that of other nearby planets, it could help scientists expand their understanding of planetary atmospheres. But right now, this is just a good guess based on data from New Horizons and a sophisticated computer model, not direct observations of the haze's composition.
segments.cn: 如果冥王星的大气层与地球以及其他邻近行星的大气层截然不同，这将有助于科学家拓展对行星大气层的 认识。但目前，这只是基于新视野号获得的数据和一个复杂计算机模型提出的合理推测，而不是对霾的成 分进行直接观测所得出的结论。

segments.en: There are other theories floating around to explain Pluto's cool temperatures, including blaming the cold air on gases in the atmosphere.
segments.cn: 关于解释冥王星低温的理论还有其他一些，包括把寒冷的空气归因于大气层中的气体。

segments.en: Luckily, the authors will get a chance to test their notions when the James Webb Space Telescope launches later. That observatory can detect different spectrums of light, which the hazy Plutonian atmosphere would be positively glowing with as it scattered sunlight. The researchers just have to wait and see if the light from the telescope validates their bright idea.
segments.cn: 幸运的是，詹姆斯·韦布空间望远镜稍后发射后，作者们将有机会检验他们的观点。这座天文台能够探测不 同光谱的光，而冥王星朦胧的大气层在散射阳光时很可能会发出大量这样的光。研究人员只需等待并观察 望远镜接收到的光是否会验证他们的这个妙想。

segments.en: Parents have a small window where they can influence their 8- to 10-year-old children's music taste, researchers have concluded. The 24-month time frame comes at an age when youngsters are old enough to appreciate poetic lyrics and snappy tunes, but have not yet started to be embarrassed by their mother and father's preferences. Dr. Hauke Egermann, a lecturer in music at the University of York, carried out a literature review into more than a dozen studies looking at parental musical influence. "Children have an openness to new music, and this means parents have an important role to play in developing the musical preferences of their kids," he said.
segments.cn: 研究人员得出结论，父母有一个短暂的窗口期，可以影响8至10岁孩子的音乐品味。这段24个月的时期处 于这样一个年龄阶段：孩子已经足够大，能够欣赏富有诗意的歌词和朗朗上口的曲调，但还没有开始因 父母的音乐偏好而感到尴尬。约克大学音乐讲师豪克·埃格尔曼博士对十多项有关父母音乐影响的研究进 行了文献综述。他说：“孩子对新音乐持开放态度，这意味着父母在培养孩子的音乐偏好方面扮演着重要 角色。”

segments.en: However, time is of the essence as parental influence is most likely to be effective during the critical time period before age ten. During adolescence, children tend to gravitate away from their parents' choices and are more influenced by their peers. A separate survey of 2,000 British parents by music streaming service Deezer also found that nearly four-fifths of parents agreed that their children were far more receptive to their musical suggestions before the age of ten. In contrast, just 10 percent of parents reported positive reactions from their teenage children when they shared their favorite music. Some 79 percent of fathers said they had tried to influence their children's music, but just 69 percent of mothers. However, mothers were more effective, with 38 percent reporting that their kids loved the tunes they shared, compared to 30 percent of dads who, in some cases, said their children cried or even fell asleep.
segments.cn: 然而，时间至关重要，因为父母的影响最有可能在十岁以前这一关键时期发挥作用。进入青春期后，孩子 往往会逐渐远离父母的选择，并更多地受到同龄人的影响。音乐流媒体服务Deezer对2000名英国父母进 行的另一项调查也发现，近五分之四的父母认为，孩子在十岁以前更容易接受他们的音乐建议。相比之 下，只有10%的父母表示，孩子进入青少年时期后，在他们分享自己喜爱的音乐时会作出积极反应。约 79%的父亲表示曾试图影响孩子的音乐选择，而母亲的这一比例仅为69%。不过，母亲的影响更有效： 38%的母亲表示孩子喜欢她们分享的曲调，而父亲中只有30%的人得到这样的反馈；有些父亲甚至表示， 孩子听着听着哭了起来，或者睡着了。

segments.en: Dr. Egermann claims introducing children to a variety of musical styles is the key to fostering good taste in later life. "By playing children a variety of genres before this critical period, research on familiarization suggests they will enjoy lots of different types of music as adults," he added. The benefits of having a wider taste in music include the ability to manage their emotions more effectively, socialize and bond with others more easily, and to have a better understanding of other cultures as well.
segments.cn: 埃格尔曼博士认为，让孩子接触各种各样的音乐风格，是培养他们日后良好音乐品味的关键。他补充说： “有关熟悉化的研究表明，在这一关键时期之前让孩子聆听多种音乐类型，他们成年后将会喜欢许多不同 种类的音乐。”拥有更广泛的音乐品味所带来的益处包括更有效地管理情绪、更容易与他人交往并建立联 系，以及更好地理解其他文化。

segments.en: Dr. Egermann advises parents not to push their favorite music too hard on their children, but instead play it as background music while a child is playing. They can also help create positive memories about artists and bands by going to concerts and live music events together.
segments.cn: 埃格尔曼博士建议，父母不要过分强迫孩子接受自己喜爱的音乐，而应在孩子玩耍时将其作为背景音乐播 放。他们还可以通过一起参加音乐会和现场音乐活动，帮助孩子对音乐家和乐队形成积极的记忆。

writing.modelEssay:
Faced with growing globalization,students realize that a deep understanding of traditional Chinese culture
helps cultivate cultural confidence. In an age when Western brands, movies and festivals flood daily life, many
young people begin to look back at their own roots. They find that cultural confidence cannot be borrowed
from outside; it must grow from real knowledge of what their ancestors created.
The reason is not hard to understand. Globalization exposes us to different values, yet it also makes us question
who we are. Only by learning the ideas behind Confucianism, the beauty of calligraphy, or the spirit of
traditional festivals can we answer that question with pride. Take the Spring Festival as an example: those who
understand its meaning of reunion and renewal celebrate it not out of habit, but out of identity.
Therefore, college students should actively read classics, visit museums and practice folk arts. The deeper we
understand traditional Chinese culture, the more confident we become in facing the world.
writing.modelCn:
面对日益增长的全球化，学生们意识到深入理解中国传统文化有助于培养文化自信。在这个西方品牌、电
影和节日充斥着日常生活的时代，许多年轻人开始回望自己的文化根脉。他们发现文化自信无法从外界借
来，而必须建立在对先辈所创造文化的真正了解之上。
其原因不难理解。全球化让我们接触到不同的价值观，但也让我们反思自己是谁。只有了解儒家思想背后
的理念、书法之美或传统节日的精神，我们才能自豪地回答这个问题。以春节为例：真正理解其团圆与更
新内涵的人，庆祝春节不是出于习惯，而是出于身份认同。
因此，大学生应积极阅读经典、参观博物馆并参与民俗艺术实践。我们对中国传统文化理解得越深入，在
面对世界时就越自信。

match.title: It's never too early to teach children about money

A.en: The cost of a mortgage or rents, meeting monthly utility bills, paying for a new car - all headaches most people get to worry about from their 20s. But while some may struggle to pay their bills after a few too many nights out at the start of the month, others will have a tightly followed plan for their repayments. So what is the difference between the shrewd saver and the more reckless spender?
A.cn: 抵押贷款或房租的费用、每月缴纳水电等生活账单、支付一辆新车的费用——这些都是大多数人从二 十多岁起就要操心的头疼事。不过，有些人可能会因为月初外出玩乐的夜晚太多而难以支付账单，另 一些人却会严格遵循还款计划。那么，精明的储蓄者与更为鲁莽的花钱者之间究竟有什么区别呢？

B.en: Experts believe it is all about the age you learn how to spend responsibly. Adult money habits are typically set by the age of seven, according to a large-scale study by the government's Money Advice Service and behaviour experts at Cambridge University. By then, most children have grasped how to recognise the value of money and are capable of complex functions such as planning ahead, delaying a decision until later and understanding that some choices are irreversible.
B.cn: 专家认为，这一切都取决于你在什么年龄学会负责任地消费。政府的金钱咨询服务机构与剑桥大学的 行为专家开展的一项大规模研究显示，成年人的金钱习惯通常在七岁时就已经形成。到那时，大多数 孩子已经掌握了如何识别金钱价值，并且能够进行一些复杂的思考，例如提前规划、将决定推迟到以 后再做，以及理解有些选择是不可逆的。

C.en: Tomorrow marks the start of Global Money Week, a worldwide initiative to help children make smart financial decisions and learn that "money matters matter". But for many young people in the UK, it's a matter of too little, too late. "The habits of mind which influence the ways children approach complex problems and decisions, including financial ones, are largely determined in the first few years of life," says Dr David Whitebread, the co- author of the study. And this core behaviour is very likely to influence their financial decisions when they are adults, he says.
C.cn: 明天将迎来全球金钱周的开始。这是一项旨在帮助儿童作出明智的财务决定，并让他们懂得“金钱问题 很重要”的全球性倡议。但对英国的许多年轻人来说，这已经是一个太少、太晚的问题。“影响儿童处 理复杂问题和作出决定，包括财务决定的思维习惯，很大程度上是在生命最初几年形成的，”该研究的 共同作者戴维·怀特布雷德博士说。他表示，这种核心行为很可能会影响他们成年后的财务决定。

D.en: The study also urges parents not to underestimate their own good and bad money habits. "Since young children have few monetary resources they control independently, it is the basic approaches and skills which are modelled, discussed and demonstrated by parents that are likely to be influential levers, breeding efficient habits and practices," it says.
D.cn: 这项研究还敦促父母不要低估自己良好或不良金钱习惯的影响。“由于幼儿能够独立支配的金钱资源很 少，因此，父母所示范、讨论和展示的基本方法与技能，很可能是促成有效习惯和做法的重要影响因 素，”研究报告称。

E.en: Parents who choose to help their children learn how to plan ahead, reflect on the past and self-regulate car make a huge difference in promoting good financial behaviour in the future, explains Whitebread. According to a survey by M&G Investments, the vast majority (83%) of parents recognise the value of teaching their children about money. However, this concern does not always carry through to practice - one in six do not feel confident enough to do it. More than one in every four parents think children should take responsibility for understanding money themselves.
E.cn: 怀特布雷德解释说，选择帮助孩子学会提前规划、反思过去并进行自我调节的父母，可以在促进孩子 未来良好财务行为方面发挥巨大作用。M&G投资公司的一项调查显示，绝大多数父母（83%）都认识 到教孩子了解金钱的价值。然而，这种关注并不总能落实到实践中——六分之一的父母觉得自己没有 足够的信心去做这件事。超过四分之一的父母认为，孩子应该自己负责了解金钱。

F.en: "There's joy in the fact that young children are spontaneous and live life in the moment, unrestrained by adult problems. But teaching children about money when they are young is a good way for parents to help them learn to delay satisfaction, so that the child thinks: 'I'd like to do this but I'm not going to.' Hard evidence suggests, if you want your child to do well in life, the earlier you can start trying to teach them inhibition and self-discipline, the better," says Whitebread, pointing to research that has shown people in prison frequently have poor impulse control, a personality trait that can affect relationships and long-term health.
F.cn: “幼儿 spontanes地生活在当下，不受成年人的烦恼束缚，这其中自有乐趣。但在孩子年幼时教他们认 识金钱，是父母帮助他们学会延迟满足的一种好方法，这样孩子就会想：‘我想做这件事，但我不会去 做。’确凿的证据表明，如果你希望孩子一生过得好，那么越早开始尝试教他们克制和自律，效果就越 好，”怀特布雷德说。他指出，有研究显示，监狱中的人往往缺乏控制冲动的能力，而这种人格特征可 能影响人际关系和长期健康。

G.en: But how should a parent try to teach their child to spend responsibly? One simple way is to give them pocket money and then help them to analyse and learn from any foolish spending decisions.
G.cn: 但是，父母应该怎样教孩子负责任地消费呢？一个简单的方法是给孩子零花钱，然后帮助他们分析并 从任何不理智的消费决定中吸取教训。

H.en: Another is through board games which can help teach financial responsibility. Pop to the Shops, a shopping board game for five-to-nine-year-olds, has been one of Orchard Toys' top 10 bestselling board games every year for the past 15 years. To win, players must use fake coins to purchase everyday grocery items from various shops around the board, and give the other players who visit their shop the correct change. If they don't have enough money, they must purchase a cheaper item. "It acts as a conversation starter about money - parents can fill in the gaps," says Orchard Toys product manager Rachael Sutcliffe.
H.cn: 另一种方法是通过棋盘游戏来帮助孩子学习财务责任感。面向五至九岁儿童的购物棋盘游戏《去商店 吧》在过去15年中每年都跻身Orchard Toys最畅销的十大棋盘游戏之列。为了获胜，玩家必须使用假 硬币，在棋盘周围的不同商店购买日常食品，并且要给到访自己商店的其他玩家找对零钱。如果钱不 够，他们就必须购买更便宜的商品。Orchard Toys的产品经理蕾切尔·萨克利夫说：“它可以成为一个 谈论金钱的开端，父母可以补充其中的不足。”

I.en: There are also some pocket-money-tracking and payment apps, such as RoosterMoney and goHenry, which are designed to be used by under-sevens, and which boast that they can help children develop good money habits. This is dependent on the children receiving enough pocket money to need an app to track their spending, which research suggests is not always the case.
I.cn: 还有一些追踪零花钱和支付的应用程序，例如RoosterMoney和goHenry，它们面向七岁以下儿童设 计，并声称能够帮助孩子养成良好的金钱习惯。不过，这取决于孩子是否能获得足够多的零花钱，以至 于需要使用应用程序来追踪支出，而研究表明，情况并不总是如此。

J.en: Surprisingly, given the research about habit-forming in young children, there are very few gaming apps that can help under-sevens - Pigby's Fair, developed by NatWest, being a notable exception. In this, children who solve basic puzzles will earn virtual money selling what they have made at different stalls in a fair, then spend or save it. But the need to shift virtual money around, and take into account interest payments and pocket money bonuses, makes it a complex financial education tool.
J.cn: 鉴于有关幼儿养成习惯的研究，令人意外的是，能够帮助七岁以下儿童学习的游戏应用程序非常少， 由NatWest开发的Pigby's Fair是一个值得注意的例外。在这款游戏中，解开基础谜题的孩子可以通过 在集市的不同摊位出售自己制作的东西来赚取虚拟货币，然后把钱花掉或存起来。不过，转移虚拟货 币、同时考虑利息支付和零花钱奖励的需要，使它成为一种复杂的金融教育工具。

K.en: There are plenty of online games which focus on coin recognition and counting with money, such as the Igloo Shopping game or Top Marks' Coins Game. So what if children find such games boring? An exciting (and free) real-world option for parents to use is a visit to Metro Bank. Although, like most banks, it does not allow children to open an account until they turn 11, it specifically tries to offer young children a chance to learn about money inside its branches by inviting kids to use the "magic money machines" to count their coins. Children who accurately guess how much was in their piggy bank (猪形储钱罐) get a prize, and free candies are handed out when the coins are exchanged for banknotes. The bank does not take a commission from the transaction.
K.cn: piggy bank( 猪形储钱罐 ) get a prize, and free candies are handed out when the coins are exchanged 有许多在线游戏专门训练儿童识别硬币以及用钱进行计算，例如Igloo Shopping游戏或Top Marks的 Coins Game。那么，如果孩子觉得这类游戏很无聊，该怎么办呢？父母可以选择一个令人兴奋且免 费的现实体验：去Metro Bank。虽然和大多数银行一样，Metro Bank不允许儿童在年满11岁之前开 户，但它专门努力为幼儿提供在银行网点内学习金钱知识的机会，邀请孩子使用“神奇点钞机”清点硬 币。准确猜出自己的猪形储钱罐里有多少钱的孩子可以获得奖品；将硬币兑换成纸币时，还会免费发 放糖果。银行不会从这笔交易中收取佣金。

L.en: At six years old, my daughter Flora is getting to grips with her finances early. She tested out a number of games aimed at teaching children her age the value of money. She enjoyed them all, but best, in her view, is Money Match Cafe, a board game where she must work out the value of different denominations (面额) of coin in her imaginary restaurant, her "customers" being her stuffed toys. "It was really fun because you get to serve food to your own toys on a little tray with a napkin on it, and then you can hug them," she says.
L.cn: 我六岁的女儿弗洛拉正在很早地学习打理自己的财务。她体验了几款旨在教同龄儿童认识金钱价值的 游戏。她喜欢所有这些游戏，但在她看来，最棒的是《Money Match Cafe》，这是一款棋盘游戏。 在游戏中，她必须在自己想象中的餐馆里算出不同面额硬币的价值，而她的“顾客”是她的毛绒玩具。 她说：“这真的很有趣，因为你可以用一个铺着餐巾的小托盘给自己的玩具上菜，然后还可以拥抱 它们。”

M.en: "If you're six and you play this game, you'll learn that you might not have the right amount of money for what you want to buy. You just have to cross your fingers and hope. It's a good challenge, and I enjoyed adding the coins up to see how much they made. But I don't like the name. Money Match Cafe is not a good name for a café. I would have liked it more if it had been Flora's Cafe or Fantastically Baked Lunches."
M.cn: “如果你六岁并且玩这款游戏，你会学到：你可能没有足够的钱买自己想要的东西。你只能祈祷并抱着 希望。这是一个很好的挑战，我喜欢把硬币加起来，看看它们总共值多少钱。但我不喜欢这个名字。 Money Match Cafe不是一个适合咖啡馆的好名字。如果它叫Flora's Cafe或Fantastically Baked Lunches，我会更喜欢。”

N.en: Seven out of ten teachers think children are now faced with financial decisions earlier. On Wednesday, Lifesavers - a new project which promotes financial education in primary schools - is hosting a conference to encourage teachers to join its programme and get free classroom resources and training. Almost two-thirds of millennials (千禧一代) wish they had received more money advice at a younger age, according to a Santander survey.
N.cn: and training. Almost two-thirds of millennials( 千禧⼀代 ) wish they had received more money advice 十分之七的教师认为，儿童现在更早就要面对财务决定。周三，Lifesavers将举办一场会议。这是一 个促进小学金融教育的新项目，旨在鼓励教师加入该项目，并获得免费的课堂资源和培训。桑坦德银 行的一项调查显示，近三分之二的千禧一代希望自己在更年轻时就接受过更多的金钱方面的建议。

O.en: Only a third of parents involve their children in discussions about their household finances, even though less than half of young people aged seven to seventeen receive financial education at school, another survey shows.
O.cn: 另一项调查显示，尽管七至十七岁的年轻人中接受过学校金融教育的不到一半，但只有三分之一的父 母会让孩子参与讨论家庭财务问题。

P.en: Most adults believe their parents have had the biggest influence on their money behaviour. So when should they start trying to instil (灌输) good habits? As early as possible before the age of seven, research suggests.
P.cn: should they start trying to instil( 灌输 ) good habits? As early as possible before the age of seven, 大多数成年人认为，父母对他们金钱行为的影响最大。那么，父母应该从什么时候开始努力灌输良好 习惯呢？研究表明，应当在七岁之前尽可能早地开始。

paragraphs.en: Three artists have brought a lawsuit against Stability AL, DeviantArt, and Midjourney, alleging that the text- to-image AI tools have infringed the rights of thousands of artists.
paragraphs.cn: 三位艺术家已对 Stability AI、DeviantArt 和 Midjourney 提起诉讼，指控这些文本生成图像的人工智能 工具侵犯了数千名艺术家的权利。

paragraphs.en: The lawsuit claims that the Stable Diffusion tool used by Stability AI, DeviantArt, and Midjourney was trained on billions of copyrighted images downloaded from the internet and used by the companies "without compensation or consent from the artists".
paragraphs.cn: 诉讼称，Stability AI、DeviantArt 和 Midjourney 使用的 Stable Diffusion 工具，是利用从互联网下载 的数十亿张受版权保护的图像进行训练的，而这些公司使用这些图像时“没有向艺术家提供补偿，也未获 得他们的同意”。

paragraphs.en: The artists are represented by The Joseph Saveri Law Firm and Matthew Butterick.
paragraphs.cn: 这些艺术家由 The Joseph Saveri Law Firm 和 Matthew Butterick 代理。

paragraphs.en: "If Stable Diffusion and similar products are allowed to continue to operate as they do now, the foreseeable result is they will replace the very artists whose stolen works power these AI products with whom they are competing," the law firm wrote in a press release. "AI image products are not just an infringement of artists' rights; they will eliminate 'artist' as a viable career path. In addition to obtaining compensation for the wrongful conduct, this lawsuit seeks to prevent that outcome and ensure these products follow the same rules as any other new technology that involves the use of massive amounts of intellectual property. If streaming music can be accomplished within the law, so can AI products."
paragraphs.cn: 该律师事务所在一份新闻稿中写道：“如果允许 Stable Diffusion 及类似产品继续以目前的方式运营，那 么可以预见的结果是，它们将取代那些为这些人工智能产品提供动力、而这些产品正与之竞争的艺术家， 而被取代的正是其作品遭到窃取的艺术家。人工智能图像产品不仅侵犯了艺术家的权利，还将使‘艺术家’ 不再是一条可行的职业道路。除了为不当行为寻求赔偿外，本诉讼还旨在阻止这一结果，并确保这些产品 遵守与任何其他涉及使用大量知识产权的新技术相同的规则。如果音乐流媒体能够在法律框架内实现，人 工智能产品也同样可以做到。”

paragraphs.en: Since text-to-image generators have increased in popularity in the past year, many artists have been vocalizing their opposition to AI art after seeing their own distorted signatures appear in AI art and finding out that their work was used to train the tools without their permission.
paragraphs.cn: 在过去一年中，随着文本生成图像工具越来越受欢迎，许多艺术家在看到自己扭曲的签名出现在人工智能 生成的艺术作品中，并发现自己的作品未经许可就被用于训练这些工具后，纷纷公开表达对人工智能艺术 的反对。

paragraphs.en: Not only are many artists furious at the possible copyright violations of AI art, but they have also been frustrated by how AI tools are able to sidestep the labor and art processes they are required to go through. As a result, many artists have been trying to ban AI art from art-sharing platforms.
paragraphs.cn: 许多艺术家不仅对人工智能艺术可能侵犯版权感到愤怒，也因人工智能工具能够绕过他们必须经历的劳动 和艺术创作过程而感到沮丧。因此，许多艺术家一直在试图禁止人工智能艺术进入艺术分享平台。

paragraphs.en: As AI innovation continues at a rapid speed, it seems that artists and lawmakers are trying to put a brake on further developments before it's too late.
paragraphs.cn: 随着人工智能创新以极快的速度持续发展，艺术家和立法者似乎正试图在为时已晚之前遏制进一步的 发展。

paragraphs.en: Many tech enthusiasts are still rallying around the promise of AI tools to create detailed images cheaply and quickly - anonymous tech supporters have already published a response to Butterick and Joseph Saveri's lawsuit on a website, using the "fair use" clause as the basis for why copyrighted images could be used by the tool.
paragraphs.cn: 许多科技爱好者仍在支持人工智能工具能够低成本、快速创作精细图像这一前景；匿名的科技支持者已经 在一个网站上发布了对 Butterick 和 Joseph Saveri 诉讼的回应，以“合理使用”条款为依据，解释为什么 这些受版权保护的图像可以被该工具使用。

paragraphs.en: Fair use, a legal doctrine that allows for a limited usage of copyrighted materials without permission by the original creators for purposes such as teaching and news sharing, is what a lot of generative model creators claim that their training data is covered by. However, since fair use applies differently to each case, it's hard to make a blanket statement about all works in a dataset as being applicable.
paragraphs.cn: 合理使用是一项法律原则，允许出于教学和新闻传播等目的，在未经原作者许可的情况下有限使用受版权 保护的材料。许多生成模型的创作者声称，他们的训练数据受到这一原则的保护。然而，由于合理使用在 不同案件中的适用方式各不相同，因此很难笼统地断言数据集中的所有作品都适用这一原则。

paragraphs.en: On a warm October morning, Daniel Agok woke up to another disappointing day at his school in Wanyjok, South Sudan. The classes he had planned teaching computer skills to aspiring young professionals were canceled, due to an unreliable diesel generator and the absence of a municipal power grid in his area. Now, he would be losing frustrated customers as well as income. Agok is just one of the hundreds of millions of people in sub- Saharan Africa, many of whom are business owners, who still do not have dependable electricity. This inequitable access to energy continues to put their livelihood and future at risk.
paragraphs.cn: 十月一个温暖的早晨，丹尼尔·阿戈克醒来时，迎接他的又是南苏丹瓦尼约克学校里令人失望的一天。由于 柴油发电机运行不稳定，而且他所在地区没有市政电网，他原本计划为有志成为年轻专业人士的人教授计 算机技能的课程被取消了。现在，他不仅会失去因失望而离去的客户，还会损失收入。阿戈克只是撒哈拉 以南非洲数亿人的代表之一，其中许多人是企业主，至今仍没有可靠的电力供应。这种不公平的能源获取 状况持续使他们的生计和未来面临风险。

paragraphs.en: The current system keeps a lid on the economic talents of people like Agok and his students. We must instead unleash their abilities and let Africa reach its true economic potential. That means wiring Africa with clean, dependable energy.
paragraphs.cn: 现行体系限制了阿戈克及其学生这类人的经济才能。相反，我们必须释放他们的能力，让非洲实现真正的 经济潜力。这意味着要用清洁、可靠的能源为非洲接入电网。

paragraphs.en: Historically, national governments on the continent have led electrification efforts, but fewer than half of the people surveyed say that the national grid is providing a reliable supply of electricity.
paragraphs.cn: 从历史上看，非洲大陆各国政府一直主导着电气化工作，但接受调查的人中，不到一半表示国家电网能够 提供可靠的电力供应。

paragraphs.en: This has led to expensive and harmful temporary "solutions". In Nigeria alone experts estimate people spend $13 billion every year on fuel for toxic, polluting generators. That number will only grow as the continent's population hits 2.5 billion people by 2050. Deploying modern grid infrastructure with speed and at scale is essential to replacing these temporary solutions with reliable and affordable alternatives.
paragraphs.cn: 这导致了昂贵且有害的临时“解决方案”。专家估计，仅在尼日利亚，人们每年就要花费130亿美元购买有 毒且污染环境的发电机燃料。随着非洲大陆人口到2050年达到25亿，这一数字只会继续增长。快速、大 规模部署现代电网基础设施，对于用可靠且价格可负担的替代方案取代这些临时解决方案至关重要。

paragraphs.en: The rapidly growing private power sector in Africa holds the key to achieving the speed and scale necessary to close the continent's energy access gap. Private companies today are building world-class infrastructure and driving forward economic growth with sustainable business models. In fact, many governments agree and have begun to embrace the private sector as partners in providing reliable power at scale. In South Africa, President Cyril Ramaphosa has streamlined licensing requirements and enlisted the private sector to play a key role.
paragraphs.cn: 非洲迅速发展的私人电力行业，是以实现弥合非洲大陆能源获取缺口所需的速度和规模的关键。如今，私 营企业正在建设世界一流的基础设施，并通过可持续的商业模式推动经济增长。事实上，许多政府对此表 示认同，并已开始接受私营部门作为合作伙伴，以大规模提供可靠电力。在南非，西里尔·拉马福萨总统简 化了许可要求，并邀请私营部门发挥关键作用。

paragraphs.en: South Africa is just one example. Across the continent, the private sector has delivered power faster and more reliably, and governments are increasingly turning to private partners.
paragraphs.cn: 南非只是其中一个例子。在整个非洲大陆，私营部门以更快的速度提供了更加可靠的电力，各国政府也越 来越多地寻求与私营合作伙伴合作。

paragraphs.en: With the right funding and structure in place, the private sector will come together to provide this essential service. After all, electrifying sub-Saharan Africa is a $350 billion opportunity.
paragraphs.cn: 只要建立适当的资金和组织架构，私营部门就会联合起来提供这项基本服务。毕竟，为撒哈拉以南非洲实 现电气化蕴含着3500亿美元的机遇。

paragraphs.en: Today, Daniel Agok is steadily growing his business in South Sudan. His town of Wanyjok was electrified by a private company, providing clean, reliable, and affordable power to his business and his neighbors. Agok now operates his growing computer skills training business smoothly. His classes are no longer affected by the smell and the constant noise of the diesel generator, and he saves money with more affordable power. His students are developing hardware and software skills.
paragraphs.cn: 如今，丹尼尔·阿戈克正在稳步发展他在南苏丹的企业。瓦尼约克镇由一家私营公司实现了电气化，为他的 企业和邻居们提供了清洁、可靠且价格可负担的电力。阿戈克现在可以顺利运营不断发展的计算机技能培 训业务。他的课程不再受到柴油发电机气味和持续噪声的影响，而且借助价格更低的电力，他节省了开 支。他的学生正在培养硬件和软件技能。
